A **group collection** is the *same* primitive as a personal saved collection (a `kind:'saved'` group, the `web10-social-saved` tag, a `saved`-service doc per saved post, the D58 `anyone` reader row for publicness) — the one difference is **who owns it**: the owner member is the **group** (its group_id, used as a `member_key`), not a user. A `provider/username` key is still normalized to the bare username (the `/groups/` marker is the discriminator — usernames are `[a-z0-9-]`). (2) **Data seam (`src/data/saved.ts`)** — `GroupIdentity` gains `owner_group`; `writeGroupIdentity` writes it; `createGroupCollection(groupId, name, { visibility })` (the group is the owner member, the slug embeds the group's slug so two groups the manager runs never collide, the face carries `owner_group`); `readGroupCollections(groupId)` (the manager's read — public + private — the tag read filtered to `owner_group === groupId`); `readGroupPublicCollections(groupId)` (the visitor's read — the D80 by-group read, filtered to `owner_group === groupId`); the personal reads (`getMyCollections` / `readUserPublicCollections`) now **skip** any collection with `owner_group` set (a group's playlists never surface on a person's profile). (3) **UI** — `GroupDetailScreen` gains a third tab **Feed | Media | Saved** (`?tab=saved`, the existing `?tab=` idiom — refresh-safe, shareable); the card grid is extracted to a shared `SavedCollectionsGrid` (one card shape, two surfaces — the profile's Saved tab + the group page); the manager (canManage) sees the tab always (even empty) + a "New collection" affordance (name → `createGroupCollection`); a visitor / member sees the tab only when the group has ≥1 **public** collection (read-only). The collection detail reuses `SavedCollectionScreen` with a group-owner check (owner = can manage the group, not `token.username === groupId`) on the new route **`/groups/:groupId/saved/:collectionId`** (the URL holds which collection is open — the "address bar is part of the product" rule); a public collection's link is shareable. `textTileColor` extracted to its own module (the shared grid + the profile both use it, no circular import). **Zero app-specific node surface (D60)** — the node stays generic; the only node change is the member-key normalization (a group_id is a universal member key, not a social concept). **Tests:** `saved.test.ts` +9 (createGroupCollection owner member + `owner_group` face + public variant; readGroupCollections manager read + the `owner_group` filter; readGroupPublicCollections by-group read + the filter + empty; the personal reads exclude group collections); `groupsScreens.test.tsx` +5 (the manager's Saved tab + "New collection" + the manager read; a non-manager with no public collections sees no tab; a non-manager with public collections sees the read-only tab; the manager creates a collection; `?tab=saved` deep link); node `test_v3_endpoints.py` +1 (a group_id member key passes through the by-user read, not stripped). 1281 web10-social green, `tsc` clean, ruff clean. fix(web10-social): **comment likes now actually register — the heart fills + the count moves on tap, and rolls back on a failed write** — operator (01.10.2026, a comment-thread screenshot): "reactions, likes dislikes not happening on comments to posts." **The root (a missing UI state update, not a data bug):** the comment-like tap fired the write (`toggleReactionKind(commentId, 'like', groups, 'comments')`) but the shared thread never updated its own `topLevel` state — no optimistic flip of `likedByMe`/`likeCount`, no re-read. The write landed on the node, but the heart stayed empty and the count stayed put until the thread was closed + reopened (a fresh read). The post-level like worked because `FeedScreen` owns `likedMap`/`likeMap` and does optimistic + rollback; the comment thread had no equivalent — the seam was documented as "optimistic + rollback on the app" (comments.md) but the app never did it. **The fix (the thread owns the node state, so the thread does the flip — `marketing/shared/discover/src/CommentThread.tsx`):** a `handleToggleLike` does the optimistic update in place — flip `likedByMe` + nudge `likeCount` (functional update, so rapid taps don't clobber), fire the writer, and roll the node back to its captured pre-tap snapshot if the write rejects (the `FeedScreen` `wasLiked` idiom). The seam type widens to `onToggleCommentLike?: (id) => void | Promise<unknown>` — the thread only awaits the returned promise for the rollback. The two social wrappers (`Feed/CommentThread.tsx` + `Feed/PostActions.tsx`) now `return` the write's promise (was `void`) so the thread can roll back on failure. **Tests:** `commentThread.test.tsx` +2 (the optimistic fill + count bump on tap, the re-tap un-like; the rollback when the write rejects). 1263 web10-social green, `tsc` clean. KB `web10-v3/social/comments.md` + the shared package doc updated (the thread owns the optimistic flip + rollback, not the app). Lane: `social-v3` in `parallel-execution.md`.

fix(marketing-ui): **the marketing People tab shows the real profile picture + banner (anon) — the same author-scoped face-prepare the social app uses, replacing the phantom media endpoint** — operator (04.10.2026, a screenshot of `dev.web10.app/trending/people`): "not seeing peoples profile pics or banners on the people tab of the marketing page". **The root (a phantom endpoint the marketing site was never fixed for):** the marketing `ProfilesBrowser` (the People tab) resolved each person's `avatar_ref`/`banner_ref` via `getPublicMediaUrl()` (`mediaPresign.ts`), which calls `POST /media/{author}/list` + `POST /media/{author}/read` — **routes that don't exist on the node** (the real media endpoints are `/v3/media/list` + `/v3/media/read-url`, both **owner-scoped** via `_user(data)` — they require a token). The marketing site reads **anon** (no token), so it can't use the owner-scoped media endpoints at all — every face resolution 404'd silently and the card fell back to the gradient banner + initial circle (exactly the screenshot). This is the *same bug class* fixed for the **social app's** People tab in 3.207.1, but the marketing site uses a different (broken) resolution path and was never fixed. **The fix (all client-side, D60 — zero node surface):** `ProfilesBrowser.tsx` resolves the page's face media through the query engine's **author-scoped face-prepare** (D73) — two batched `POST /v3/query` reads (one per face field) over the page's authors, `SELECT author_key, body FROM profile WHERE author_key IN (…)`, scoped to each user's followers group (`{API_HOST}/groups/users/{username}/followers`, the I3 gate) with `prepare: { face: { bodyField: 'body', mediaField: 'avatar_ref'|'banner_ref', urlField: … } }`. The engine mints the face URL **bound to the row's `author_key`** (not the viewer), so it works for any reader — **anon included** — the same mechanism the social app's `people.ts` `resolveFaces` uses. A face the reader can't read (a private profile) is absent → that card keeps the gradient fallback; a failure degrades the whole page to faceless cards, never a throw. The `getPublicMediaUrl` import is dropped from the component (it remains for `FeedPreview.tsx`). **The group face (honest, not fixed):** a group's face media is a bare `public_media` doc owned by the group owner (not attached to any group), so there is **no anon presign path** for it — the owner-scoped media endpoints need a token, and the anon-capable `/v3/media/thumbnail` 404s on a media doc with no group attachment. The old code called the same phantom endpoints (always failed → gradient), so group cards keep the gradient fallback; `readGroupFace` now keeps only the rich name (the dead media presign is removed) with a comment pinning the gap (the node would need to attach `public_media` docs to the discover board for an anon presign seam). **Tests:** `Trending.test.tsx` +2 (a person with an avatar/banner ref renders the real `<img>` via the face-prepare — and the read is the author-scoped face-prepare scoped to the followers group, not the owner-scoped media endpoint; a faceless person renders the gradient with no face-prepare read). 284 marketing-ui green, `tsc -b` clean. Lane: `discover-ia-consistency` in `parallel-execution.md`.
fix(web10-social): **"New group" on the People tab 403s ("no write access to the requested group") instead of opening the draft — the client built the group id the node never created** — operator (04.10.2026, a People-tab screenshot): "on the people tab when i hit new group, gives me this error... instead of making me create the group." **The root (a group-id shape the client and node disagree on):** the node's `create_group` derives the id as `{provider}/groups/users/{creator}/{slug}` (api/app/v3/endpoints/groups.py:144-145 — the `users/` segment landed in D53 bite 2, 15a5bb83) and **returns it**. But the client's `createCommunityGroup` ignored that return value and built its own id via `communityGroupId()` = `web10.app/groups/{owner}/{slug}` (no `users/`, hardcoded `web10.app`) for the face write (`groups.ts` → `writeGroupIdentity`). So the face doc was attached to a group id the node never created → the author is not a member of it → `can_write_group` is false → the D58 write gate 403s with "no write access to the requested group" (`documents.py:168`). The group *contract* was created fine (the `Cool Group` card in the screenshot); only the face write — and therefore the whole "open the draft in edit mode" handoff — failed. **The fix (two parts, `groups.ts`, D60-clean — zero node surface):** (1) `createCommunityGroup` now uses the **node's returned `group_id`** for the face write (and its return value) instead of a client-reconstructed id — the node is the source of truth, so a provider/shape drift can never re-open the hole; (2) `communityGroupId` now builds the node's created-group shape `{provider}/groups/users/{owner}/{slug}` (provider from the token via `currentProvider()`, the same derivation the followers / close-friends groups already use) so the create-time slug guard (`slugTaken`) checks the right id. **Tests:** `groupsDraft.test.ts` / `groupsCreate.test.ts` / `groupsFilter.test.ts` re-pinned to the `api.localhost/groups/users/jacoby149/…` shape (the test token's provider); the `createGroup` mocks now mirror the node's derivation. 1268 web10-social green, `tsc` clean.

fix(web10-social): **a markdown post's link preview stops leaking `**` / `#` / `[]()` / ``` — the OG card's text is stripped to plain words (D85, the client-side "one touch")** — the post body is markdown (D85), and the social app's link-preview card (`preview/card.mjs`) put the raw `doc.body.text` straight into the card's `title` + `description` — so a post with a heading, bold, a link, or a code block leaked its markdown syntax into the OG / Twitter-card preview that crawlers render. **The touch is client-side, zero node surface (D60-clean):** the node's `share.py` was deleted in 3.91.0 — the card is now built in the social app's preview server, so the fix lives there, not in the node. **The build:** (1) a tiny generic **markdown → plain-text strip util** (`preview/markdown.mjs`, `stripMarkdown`) — "render this string as plain words": bold / italic / strikethrough / heading / link→text / inline + fenced code / list / blockquote → the words, the syntax gone. It is generic, not a social concept (any app can flatten a markdown string), pure + small so it is unit-testable, and degrades gracefully (a plain-text pre-markdown string is unchanged; unrecognized syntax passes through). **Emphasis is only stripped when the markers FLANK the words directly** (no whitespace inside the markers, per CommonMark) — so intentional literal `**` / `***` / `* word *` / `!` / `2 * 3 * 4` show exactly as the user typed them, while real `**bold**` / `*ital*` is still stripped. fix(web10-social): **the post lightbox stops showing two sets of side arrows on a multi-frame post opened from the profile grid** — operator (01.10.2026, a profile lightbox screenshot of a 2-image post): "seeing two sets of side arrows here, weird!". **The root (two nav systems, one screen, both drawing chevrons):** the profile grid opens `PostLightbox` with the Instagram-style `onPrevPost`/`onNextPost` seam (3.176.0), which renders backdrop arrows (`post-lightbox-prev-post`/`-next-post`) that step through the PROFILE'S posts. The keyboard handler already had the same precedence (post-nav wins over media paging), so touch + keyboard now agree. The in-pane arrows are untouched on surfaces without post nav (the permalink, the group media lightbox, the single-post profile — the carousel keeps its arrows there). **Tests:** `profileLightboxPostNav.test.tsx` +1 regression (a 2-frame post on a 2-post profile → post-nav arrows present, in-pane media arrows absent, frame counter present) — fails pre-fix. 1252 web10-social green, `tsc` clean. feat(shared) + test(web10-social) + docs(kb): **the hover preview gets its mobile analog — a scroll-dwell preview on touch devices (the "phone version of hovering")** — operator (30.09.2026): "on desktop hovering a video with mouse plays it. but on mobile hovering with finger when you are scrolling doesnt play … youtube mobile all the other mobile experiences have a phone version of hovering over and the video starting, then it stays played, then detects again a little later it is a mobile kind of a analog to the hover with mouse on desktop". **The gap:** the E1–E4 hover preview (`HoverVideo`, `@web10/discover`) keyed off `mouseenter`/`mouseleave` — and a phone never fires `mouseenter`, so the mobile tile was a dead static thumbnail (the E1 spec explicitly said "touch keeps the static thumbnail"). **The build (one shared component, both apps — `marketing/shared/discover/src/HoverVideo.tsx`, zero node surface, D60):** the same preview machine now takes a second input path — a **scroll dwell**: the preview plays when the finger **stops** over a tile that is **≥60% in view** (an IntersectionObserver on the frame), keeps playing (looping) while the tile stays in view + the finger is idle, and stops the **moment the user scrolls** (a global `scroll`/`touchmove`/`resize` listener cancels the preview immediately + arms a **300ms** dwell timer — the "detects again a little later" re-arm). A **module-level coordinator** arbitrates across the wall: each tile registers + reports its visibility ratio, and the coordinator **elects the most visible eligible tile — one preview at a time** (a wall of cards scrolling by does not mint N live previews); a winner scrolled below the threshold loses immediately. Touch detection is `matchMedia('(hover: none) and (pointer: coarse)')` (jsdom-safe → the desktop path is untouched). Both inputs feed the **same `hovered` value, computed at render time** (`pointerHover || (isTouch && inView && dwell)`) — no derived-state effect (a state update from an effect is an extra render hop the play/pause effect must not depend on; under fake timers the re-render lands a commit late and the play never fires — the anti-pattern the KB now names). Screenshots: `discover-home-dwell-{desktop,375}.png` (the wall renders clean at rest — the dwell itself is a live gesture, unit-tested). feat(api) + feat(sdk) + feat(deploy) + test: **the TURN relay — WebRTC P2P works across NAT, not just on open networks** — operator (30.09.2026), after the 3.185.0 ping/pong work: "webrtc still showed friend online but me offline … even though we did some stuff to supposedly make things more robust … on the messages they werent refreshing for him but were for me" → "okay, make the turn server please!" **The root (the one ping/pong couldn't fix):** 3.185.0 fixed a real *in-app* one-way bug (the SDK dropped the outbound channel's `data` event), but the operator's symptom is a **network-level** failure. The ICE config was STUN-only (5 Google STUNs, no TURN anywhere in the deploy). STUN only hole-punches, and that fails behind a symmetric NAT, CGNAT (most mobile networks), or a firewall that blocks inbound UDP — the channel goes **one way**: the more-open peer reaches the walled one (sees it green, messages land) but not vice-versa (the walled one sees the other gray, messages don't refresh). Ping/pong can't fix this — a round trip can't succeed over a wall that blocks one direction. **The build (node mints, client consumes, D60-clean):** (1) **`POST /ice`** (`api/app/endpoints/system.py`) — next to `/certify`, the same gate (a token, `certify` I2). Returns the STUN set always + a **TURN server with a freshly-minted RFC 8484 time-limited credential** (username = expiry timestamp, credential = base64 HMAC-SHA1 of the username under `TURN_SECRET`) only when `TURN_URL` + `TURN_SECRET` are set. The secret never leaves the node. (2) **`getIceServers()`** (`sdk/src/v3.ts`) — the client seam; the `rtc` module's `initP2P` now calls it (when no explicit `iceServers` passed) instead of the static STUN default, falling back to the default if the fetch fails. A **saved post** is a doc in an app-named **`saved`** service that `ref_value`s the target post's `doc_id` (a pointer, not a copy). Because posts, videos, and shorts are all one `posts` doc, **one save covers all three** — no separate "saved videos" / "saved shorts" machinery. **The privacy model (the load-bearing call, the "sensitive" guard):** publicness *is* a role grant to a principal class (D58, `groups/access.md`) — no separate "visibility" flag on the node. A collection's **membership is the privacy boundary**: **private by default** = owner row only (a non-owner's content read 403s, I3 — a stranger on the profile sees the collection's *face* but not its contents); **public** = the app adds the `(G, 'anyone', 'reader')` row via `addGroupMember` (the *same call* that makes a profile public). **The surface (the operator's "A"):** a **Saved** tab on the profile (`/u/:username?tab=saved`, the existing `Posts | Media` tabs + this one, the `?tab=` deep-link idiom) — the YouTube-channel "Playlists" shape — listing the user's collections as **cards** (cover, name, "N items"); a card opens `/u/:username/saved/:collectionId` (deep-linkable) rendering the saved posts as the profile's own wall/feed. A **Save** post action ("Save to…") writes into a collection (owner-of-the-token only, anon-hidden). **The line it does not cross (D60 / I3):** the node stays generic (a notes app wants "saved notes," a music app "saved tracks" — same group+`ref_value`+role-grant composition, different service name); a `ref_value` is **not a grant** (resolving a saved ref runs the target post's *own* read gate, so a private post from someone else stays private even inside your collection); `kind: 'saved'` is a render hint, never a security boundary. Rejects: a node-side "saved" table/endpoint (D60 reject), a flat single "watch later" list (the operator's framing is *named collections*), and public-by-default (the "sensitive" framing + the privacy model both point private-by-default). **The build (all client-side, `social-v3` lane):** the data seam (`src/data/saved.ts`), the Saved tab on the profile, the collection detail view, the "Save to…" post action, and the e2e gauntlet (the I3 anti-test: a non-owner reads a *private* collection and gets 403 / a *public* one and gets the posts; a dead ref degrades). KB: `social/saved-collections.md`.

feat(api) + feat(sdk) + feat(web10-social) + test + docs(kb) + ops: **the "dead groups" fix — groups the operator created but could no longer edit or delete are healed, and deleting a group is now one tap in the My Groups list** — operator (30.09.2026): "i dont see any way to delete groups, also some groups i created that arent letting me edit them, just dead groups. we should make some kind of healing that deletes them, you can check it out on the ubuntu deployment node." **The root (found in the prod + dev ClickHouse, a member-key format mismatch):** the social app created community groups with the owner member row under the FULL form (`web10.app/users/{username}`), but the node resolves the acting user to the **bare username** (`_user` → the JWT `username` claim) on every read/write path. So the client's `owner` row was never matched by the node's permission checks, and the node's `create_group` — not finding the bare-username creator among the passed members — added `{username} → admin`, a role that is **not defined in the community contract** (owner / moderator / page-curator / member / reader). The creator's resolvable role therefore granted no `manageRoles` / `deleteGroup` → the group was a member-only ghost: it showed in My Groups but the Edit pencil, the kebab, and the delete never appeared. Confirmed dead on the box: dev `boxin-club` + `new-group` (`admin` + orphaned `owner`), prod `boxin-club` (orphaned `owner`, no bare row) + `e-sports-grinders` (bare row `member` + orphaned `owner`). **The fix, in four layers:** (1) **Root cause (client, `groups.ts`)** — `createCommunityGroup` / `ensureCommunity` now write the owner row under the **bare username** (matching the node's `_user` convention and the already-working followers group), so new groups are owned from birth. (2) **Node ownership guarantee (`api`)** — `create_group` replaces the broken `admin` fallback with a new `ensure_creator_owner(group_id, creator, roles)`: the creator (the `{creator}` segment of the group_id) is re-pointed to the `owner` role if the contract defines one (no-op for owner-less groups like DMs, and when already owner). The node is now correct by construction regardless of the member-key form a client sends. (3) **The self-heal (`api` + `sdk` + client)** — a new `POST /v3/groups/heal-owner` (gated on creator == caller, idempotent) runs `ensure_creator_owner`; the SDK exposes `healGroupOwner`; the social app calls it on load (My Groups list + group detail) whenever a group the user created is not manageable, then re-reads — so a dead group becomes editable/deletable again the moment it's opened, no operator intervention. (4) **The delete affordance (`web10-social`)** — the My Groups list rows now carry a **Delete** action for owners (a two-tap confirm, the same idiom as the kebab's published-delete), so removing a group no longer requires digging into group detail → kebab → Roles. **Live data:** the 4 dead groups on the ubuntu box (dev + prod) were healed directly in ClickHouse (an additive `creator → owner` row — the same minimal fix the code now does); see `ubuntu-deployment/OPS-LOG.md`. **Tests:** node `test_v3_clickhouse.py` `TestEnsureCreatorOwner` (4: no-owner-role no-op, already-owner no-op, non-owner re-point, missing-row add) + `test_v3_endpoints.py` `TestHealGroupOwner` (3: creator heals, non-creator 401, not-found 404); SDK `v3.test.ts` +2 (`healGroupOwner` posts `groups/heal-owner` + surface); web10-social `groupsScreens.test.tsx` +5 (list heal-on-load + re-read, no-heal for non-created, delete two-tap, non-owner shows Leave not Delete, detail heal-on-load + no-heal) and the create-flow tests re-pinned to the bare-username owner row. 1064 api + 1180 web10-social + 153 sdk green; ruff + tsc clean. fix(api): **the WebRTC signaling gate — `POST /certify` parity restore (P2P was dead on every non-local node)** — operator (29.09.2026), on the real-time P2P (notifications + messaging): "i am not convinced anything on the app works real time … not clear that the bid with the ice server is 2 way" + "the issue was it was implemented in JS, we switched to python, and didnt get parity with all the functionality didnt implement certify, oyy vey." **The root (a v2→v3 migration gap, not a P2P bug):** the RTC signaling server (`api/rtc/index.ts`, written in the v1/v2 era) calls `POST https://{provider}/certify` on **every** connection and keeps the socket only on a 200 — anything else closes it. `/certify` existed on the v2 JS node but was **dropped in the Python rewrite** (the v3 lane notes even record it: "legacy `/signup` + removed `/certify`"). So over real HTTPS the signaling server 404'd and **closed every socket** — no peer ever stayed registered, so `initP2P` looked like it connected but P2P (real-time DMs + notifications + presence) was **completely dead on any non-local node**. **Why it masked itself locally (the corrupted measure):** the local API is HTTP-only (port 80), so the RTC server's `https://api.localhost/certify` call **fails at the network layer** (no TLS) → axios *rejects* → the server has **no `.catch()`**, so `close()` is never called → the socket stays open → P2P "works." The e2e P2P gauntlets (`social-p2p.spec.ts`, `social-notifications.spec.ts`) are green **for the wrong reason** — they pass because the environment accidentally bypasses the gate, not because the gate works. **The fix (node, generic — a core auth endpoint, not an app concept; D60-clean):** `POST /certify` (`api/app/endpoints/system.py`) runs the existing `services/auth.certify` — signature verification (I2, no unsigned decode), provider match (the token is from this node), and expiry — and returns 200 on success, 401 otherwise. The signaling server then keeps the socket only for a genuinely valid token, and the gate's `jwt.decode`-without-verify hole (it trusted the `provider`/`username` claims) is closed because the only thing it relied on now actually verifies. **Tests:** `api/tests/test_certify_endpoint.py` (6: valid → 200; expired / malformed / cross-provider / forged → 401; missing → anon 200, faithful to the service). 1051 api tests green, `ruff` clean. **The passive-receiver model the operator asked about is already correct** (only the sender actively connects; the recipient just needs the app open — `initP2P` runs app-wide on sign-in, and the notification store subscribes to the P2P bus from any screen); this was the one thing actually broken. **Follow-up (filed, `notifications (D69)` lane):** harden the e2e gauntlets so they can't pass on the network-failure path (witness the certify 200, or run the API over TLS in e2e) — otherwise the next regression ships green.

docs(strategy): **the multi-node "how" doc (`multi-node.md`) + the read model decided (client-side fan-out) + the I6 security invariant + the end-state vision (reads are the business model)** — operator (29.09.2026), the design conversation after D84 (3.181.1): "actually first dont we need to talk about how multi node even works? user hits both nodes to read / if following both? pulls feed from both providers and the social ui mixes up the feeds? or what?" + "does one node query the other node, or does the user query both nodes?" + "does clickhouse support joining from another clickhouse? because it could straight up mix like that, introduces a lot of potential vulnerability so need to be careful there" + "could have a user follow a user on another node, then joins work unexpectedly … a contrived ClickHouse in Node B set up perfectly to steal from Node A when doing multi node query." **The new doc** (`knowledge/strategy/multi-node.md`) is the authoritative "how" reference (the "what/why" is D84, the "what/why" for token verification is D7). **The read model (decided):** (1) **client-side fan-out for v1** — the user's client (holding the home-node token) queries each node the user follows people on (targeted by provider, not broadcast) and does a ranked merge of the result sets; **server-side proxy is deferred** (node-to-node trust + a confused-deputy cache risk — a cache key that omits the reader principal leaks one user's read to another). (2) **The linchpin:** you do NOT need an account on the other node — following bob on B from home node A is a *cross-node membership* (a member row on B's followers group with `member_key = A/users/alice`), not a cross-node account; the identity is *verified, not registered*, on B. (3) **The cross-node boundary is the HTTP API + a JWKS-verified token — never the database.** ClickHouse's `remote()`/`cluster()` are for *trusted clusters* (shared schema, nodes you operate) and are **rejected** for federation (a DB-level trust path that bypasses the API's auth). **I6 (new invariant):** the cross-node boundary is the HTTP API + a verified token; **no node ever queries another node's ClickHouse**; **remote data is content, never control** (never query input, never a key into the local ClickHouse, never a grant — the feed merge is a result-set *union* of independently I3-authorized reads). **The "mine Node A from Node B" attack fails** because every read is re-authorized by the *serving* node against the *verified* token — a data reference is not a grant (the same property that stops a local user reading other posts, I3); there is no multi-node query for B's ClickHouse to influence. **D84 updated:** the read model is now *decided* (was "open, to be discussed"), I6 added to the invariants, the "rejects" list gains cross-ClickHouse federation, and the seam references `multi-node.md`. **The end-state vision (added, operator: "the v2 you're proposing is all that is needed honestly, because reads are profitable, reads carry the node adds etc."):** the read layer is the **business model** — a node earns from serving reads, node-ads (D57) ride with reads. **The user is on A** (their home node / session), so **A serves the ads for the user's session and keeps the majority of their ad revenue** (not because of any content proportion, but because the user is on A); a foreign node (B) keeps the ad revenue from the content it serves. It works cross-node without the node holding the viewer's data because node-ads are operator-curated, not user-targeted (no PII crosses the boundary — readable-by-design, I4). **The "feel like one node" spectrum:** v1 (decided) read fan-out; **v2 (the unification target, all that's needed) cross-node engagement aggregation** — a *global* like/comment count via API-layer read aggregation (each node's ClickHouse fast-scans local engagement, the API merges, the client shows an eventually-consistent unified count) — enabled by readable-by-design; **v3 (the wall, not a phase) cross-node write unification** — a strongly-consistent global counter across two independent nodes, where ClickHouse's model (no consensus/transactional store) says no; **F (a natural outcome, not a phase) ads** — no settlement, no Stripe, no cut for routing: **the user is on A** (their home node / session), so **A serves the ads for the user's session and keeps the majority of their ad revenue** — not because of any content proportion, but simply because the user is on A; a foreign node (B) keeps the ad revenue from the content it serves. It falls out of "the user is on their home node" + "ads ride with reads" (D57) — nothing to build. **Lane** (`multi-node-federation (D84)`) updated: D is decided (client-side fan-out), **E (engagement aggregation) added**, the plan points at `multi-node.md`, I6 noted. No code change this entry — decision + plan only.

docs(strategy): **D84 — multi-node federation: one canonical principal format + the foundation (decision + lanes, no code)** — operator (29.09.2026), after the profile Following-tab fix (3.179.1) exposed the member_key format drift: "this doesnt sound good, because the full provider/username should be used, what if eventually people follow two same usernames on different providers?" → "you should do it right now! make it work multi provider, this is the main hangup that stops it from doing so" → "we need to make the multi node thing possible, set the foundation, we don't need to show it working right away, but yes we should be reading the other node's feed some day, multi node feed absolutely, but there is more we need to discuss about how that would work. i.e. does one node query the other node, or does the user query both nodes (the node they're on and the node they're not on)?" **The decision (recorded in `knowledge/strategy/decisions.md` D84):** web10 is a **federation of nodes**, not one node. The foundation is (1) a **single canonical principal format** across the whole identity layer and (2) **cross-node token verification** (D7 / I1 — already in flight). **The hangup (the current state):** the node is architecturally single-node and the identity layer is **inconsistent** — the same user is `jacoby149` in `documents.author_key` + followers `group_members.member_key` but `web10.app/users/jacoby149` in community/DM `member_key` (DM even hardcodes `web10.app`); there is **no `provider` column**, the provider is either omitted or crammed into the string. `import_worker.py` already checks **both** forms because it can't tell which a group used; the 3.179.1 `/by-user` Following-tab fix is one symptom, not the disease. **The canonical format (the load-bearing call):** one column, **`{provider}/users/{username}`**, chosen across `author_key` + every `member_key` + the reader principal (not just `group_members`). **Why one column, not two** (the operator asked): ClickHouse has no UNIQUE constraints so two columns buy no integrity, they break the principal classes (`anyone`/`authenticated`/`anon` have no provider → a sentinel), and a two-column `ORDER BY` forces a table rebuild; one column keeps the read gate a plain equality JOIN and makes the migration data-only. **The four phases (the foundation, in order — each its own PR/lane):** **A** the canonical principal format + data migration (gates C, D); **B** cross-node token verification (D7/I1, independent of A but both needed before C); **C** cross-node group membership (following someone on another node = joining *their* followers group on *their* node); **D** cross-node reads (the multi-node feed) — **open, a discussion not a decision**: (1) **client-side fan-out** (the client holds tokens for both nodes, queries each, merges — matches the existing Cross-Node Addressing SDK seam, the node stays a dumb broker, I3 stays local) vs (2) **server-side proxy** (the home node queries the other and merges — one-node client, but imports the node-to-node trust D7 rejects). The lean is (1) + targeted routing (the KB's "targeted queries, not broadcasts"). **What it rejects:** a `provider` column; leaving the format drift (the 3.179.1 normalization is a stopgap that Phase A reverses); building the read path before the canonical format + token verification; a global one-database federation. **No code change this entry** — decision + lanes only. **Lane:** `multi-node-federation (D84)` in `parallel-execution.md` (A/B/C/D + the `api2.localhost` two-node test harness H).

The board is settled via the API (`waitForPostsOnBoard`) before the wall loads, since the wall reads the board once on mount (ClickHouse eventual consistency). The open tab (Video / Shorts / Hot Gossip / People) was a separate surface that only learned the query via Enter / the "see all" CTA. The operator wants the field to be the tab's search box: picking a category OPENS the tab, and typing live-filters whatever tab is open. **The build (all client-side, `GlobalSearch.tsx` — no node change, D60):** (1) **A category tap opens the tab** — tapping People / Video / Shorts / Hot Gossip in the dropdown navigates to that destination (`/people` / `/video` / `/shorts` / `/hot-gossip`) carrying the query (`?q=`); Enter / the "see all" CTA do the same (they were already S8's behavior — now the tap matches them). The tap no longer just flips the preview. (2) **The field is the open tab's live filter** — when one of the four search destinations is the current route, the field mirrors the tab's `?q=` (deep-link + refresh-safe — the URL is the source of truth) and typing writes the debounced query back to the tab's URL as `?q=` (`replace`, no history spam per keystroke); the destination's existing `?q=` client-side filter (DiscoverScreen / ShortsWall / DiscoverExploreTab) reacts to the URL change and filters live. The X clears the field AND the tab's `?q=` (the tab un-filters). On any non-destination route (feed, profile, messages) the field is the front door only — the preview shows, no `?q=` is written (a `?q=` on `/feed` would be noise). (3) **The mode follows the open tab** — the dropdown's preview matches the tab being filtered (on `/video` it previews Video, on `/hot-gossip` it previews Hot Gossip, …); on a non-destination route it rests on People (S7: the search is people-first). **The interaction guard (the subtle part):** the `?q=` write is gated on the field being focused AND on a real interaction (a keystroke or the X clear) — never on mount or a bare focus — so a deep link (`/video?q=…`) is not wiped before the field seeds from it, and a navigation (a row tap) ends the live-filter gesture (the field re-seeds from the new URL). The X clear removes `?q=` directly (robust to the mousedown-blur a real browser fires before the click). **Tests:** `globalSearch.test.tsx` re-pinned to the S9 model — the four "toggle flips" cases become "on the {tab} the dropdown previews {tab}" (the mode follows the open tab); the three "Enter in {mode}" cases become "Enter on the {tab}"; the three "tapping a category" cases assert the tap NAVIGATES to the destination with `?q=`; the row-tap cases drop the now-redundant mode-people click (People is the default) and the short-row case moves onto the Shorts tab; +8 new S9 cases (typing on each of the four tabs writes `?q=` debounced; the field seeds from the tab's `?q=`; the X clears the field AND the tab's `?q=`; typing on a non-destination route writes no `?q=`; Enter on an open tab stays on the tab). 1124 web10-social tests green, `tsc` clean. **No node change (D60 — entirely client-side).** **KB:** `global-search.md` S9 + `plan.md` S9.

As long as you act fast, you are legally protected while you are small. we need this on the app for compliance." **The model (all client-side + a doc — zero node surface, D60):** a copyright takedown is a *legal-compliance* surface, not a platform feature. A rights holder emails the **designated agent** (`copyright@web10.com` for the reference node / web10-social; a self-hosted node names its own in its own terms) with a link to the infringing content; the operator opens the link and removes it manually (the existing board takedown `POST /v3/groups/hide`, or the author's own delete). Acting fast on valid notices is the small-node legal protection. **The build:** (1) **The in-app affordance — a `mailto:` composer, not a write** (`marketing/web10-social/src/components/shared/ReportCopyright.tsx`): a dialog showing the agent's email (with a copy button) + a pre-filled message (the content's link, the author, a rights statement, name/contact/good-faith fields) that hands off to the user's mail client. It never sends anything itself — no data write, no node call (D60: the node stays generic). **One always-reachable entry point, not a per-post button on every surface** (video / shorts / hot gossip / profile / lightbox) — the mechanism is an email, so the button lives in **Settings → About → Report copyright** (`SettingsScreen.tsx`, next to "Report a bug"), not scattered across the content surfaces. The dialog is post-aware (a surface can pass the post's permalink) but the canonical entry is the general one. (2) **The terms of service** (`marketing/marketing-ui/public/docs/terms.md` — new) — the user-facing terms: your data is yours, the node is readable by design (D41), the content-blind telemetry model (D56), and the **Copyright & DMCA** section (the agent email + the 3-step takedown + the in-app entry point). fix(web10-social) + test(web10-social): **the watch page stops its "sick spammy loop" — a re-render/re-load runaway that hammered the node into 429s and left the video stuck on the skeleton** — operator pass (29.09.2026, watch page stuck loading with only one video on the node): "this is having trouble loading, there is only one video on the platform, but it should still work" + "in some kind of sick spammy loop". **The root (a fresh-object in the `useCallback`/`useEffect` dep chain):** `WatchScreen` read `const token = getWapi().readToken()` at render scope and put that `token` in the `load` `useCallback`'s deps — but the SDK's `readToken()` returns a **fresh object every call** (`decodeJwt` builds a new one, `sdk/src/v3.ts`), so `load` was a new function on **every render**, and `useEffect(() => { void load(); }, [load])` re-ran every render → `load()` → `setLoading(true)` + state writes → re-render → repeat forever. The `?t=` write-back made it worse: each write changed `searchParams` → a fresh `knobState` object (the `useMemo` re-parsed on every `searchParams` change) → another fresh `load` → another full re-read of the post + board + media + engagement. On a one-video node the board read is cheap, so the loop ran at full speed until the node's rate limiter kicked in — the console showed `load — post:` + `hls player — attach`/`destroy` repeating, then `POST /v3/query 429 (Too Many Requests)`. The existing `watchScreen.test.tsx` masked it: its `getWapi` mock returned a **stable** token object, so the old dep never churned. **The fix (the ShortsScreen idiom — read the token inside the callback, key the effect on stable primitives):** `load` now reads the token inside itself (`const token = getWapi().readToken()`, the same pattern `ShortsScreen` uses) and parses `knobState` from the stable `?knobs=` string inside itself; the URL state is derived as **stable primitives** (`knobsKey = searchParams.get('knobs')`, `relatedness` a string) instead of fresh objects; the `load` deps are `[postId, knobsKey, relatedness]` — all stable. The effect now re-runs only when the video (`postId`) or the ranking/relatedness actually changes — not on every render, and **not** on `?t=` write-backs (which change `searchParams` but leave `knobsKey`/`relatedness` untouched, so the video keeps playing). The outer render-scope `token` is kept only to derive `isAnon` (a stable boolean, not a dep). **Tests:** new `watchScreen.test.tsx` regression — re-points the `getWapi` mock so `readToken` returns a **fresh object each call** (reproducing the real SDK) and asserts the board is read ≤3 times after the page settles (the old code read it **190×** in the same window, verified red against the reverted deps). 1070 web10-social green, `tsc` clean. Lane: `watch-page` in `parallel-execution.md`.

The sweep is **service-agnostic** (no `posts` hardcode — "take this user off the board" is a board op, whatever service the doc lives in). This fixes "I hid the user but their posts are still visible" — the hide now takes effect immediately, not on the user's next post. (2) **The node-level ban** — a new `node_config.banned_users` (a JSON array of usernames, the same shape as `auto_hide_users`), admin-only `POST /v3/moderation/ban`. A banned user's content is **filtered out of every read path**: the board read (`_board_base_sql`, threaded from the `/v3/read` + group-detail endpoints via a new `config.banned_users()` safe helper) and the query engine (`_boundary_cte_sql`) both carry an `author_key NOT IN (banned_users)` predicate — so a banned user's docs do not surface in any read (discover, feed, the D73 query engine) for any service. The ban is **generic** (a node-owner feature, not scoped to social), **node-local** (a node_config list, not a user property — it does not follow the user across nodes), and **reversible** (remove the username and their content returns). It is stronger than the hide: a hide is board curation (their profile + followers' feed are intact), a ban reaches the whole read path. feat(sdk) + feat(web10-social) + feat(ui) + test + docs(kb): **the app owns its own contracts — a universal contract-reconciliation primitive + the consensual self-heal that fixes the "owner absent from the people directory" bug (and a clobbering bug found while scrutinizing it)** — operator: "hmm something is wrong with the people tab, should have people there are plenty of people on here" + "i in fact thought we fixed this" + "yourself should show up in your people results no use in filtering yourself out" + "does the social app detect my contracts are stale and ask me to update them or no?" + "build the healing please! should be consensual healing by the app, app is supposed to always heal, i.e. check every contract needed for a working app, if not hard == equals, then suggest a change" + "lets do something more durable here! even could be done as an improvement to the sdk, it checks the differences, improvement to the authenticator, fully" + "add to the knowledge base this stuff on the self healing design! just want it to be robust so really look at it, scrutinize, to make sure we are covering all the ways it could break". **The root (verified against a live node):** a group contract is app infrastructure, and it can DRIFT silently. The operator's followers group was created **before** the `reader` role was added to the canonical `FOLLOWER_ROLES` — it carries the `anyone → reader` member row but the contract's `roles` array has only `owner` + `member` (no `reader`). The node's read gate resolves a grant by looking up the role the member row **names**; an undefined role grants nothing, so the public-profile grant is **inert** and the owner is absent from the D0 people directory (no error, no crash — the feature just quietly stops working). A group created after the role shipped has all three and works — same app, same code, the difference is purely contract age. **A second bug found while scrutinizing (a clobber):** the first-cut public-by-default heal re-added the `anyone` row on sign-in if missing, but making a profile **private** is implemented by *removing* the `anyone` row (`setProfilePublic(false)` → `removeGroupMember`) — so the heal and the user's choice fought: make private → sign out → sign in → the heal re-adds `anyone` → profile public again, against the user's will. **The design (KB: `groups/contract-healing.md`, the canonical reference):** the **SDK provides the mechanism** (a universal "diff a group contract against a canonical spec, heal the diff" primitive — it knows nothing about followers/profiles/social), the **app provides the canonical spec** (web10-social declares `FOLLOWERS_CONTRACT_SPEC`), the **node stays generic** (D60). The heal is **consensual** — additive, never destructive: it only ADDS what is missing (a role, a permission op, a member row, a tag) + resets a drifted join policy, and it only touches what the spec declares (anything the owner set that the spec doesn't mention is left as-is). The load-bearing split is the **app's**: it puts **infrastructure** in the spec (the role definitions, the open join policy, the followers tag — things the app needs and the owner doesn't meaningfully choose) but **not** the **`anyone` publicness row** (the owner's choice — a create-time default + `setProfilePublic` toggle). So the missing `reader` role self-heals on the next sign-in (the inert grant starts working, the owner reappears in the directory) **without** the heal ever clobbering the owner's publicness choice. **The build:** (1) **SDK** (`sdk/src/v3.ts`) — `diffGroupContract(spec, current)` (pure: `missingRoles` / `rolePermissionGaps` / `missingMembers` / `joinPolicyDrifted` / `missingTags` / `inSync`), `mergeGroupRolesForReconcile` (pure: the full merged role list — `updateGroup` *replaces* the roles field, so the delta alone would erase the owner's roles), `reconcileGroupContract(groupId, spec)` (client method: getGroup + getGroupMembers → diff → additive heal, idempotent, returns the diff + whether it healed), and `findDanglingGrants(roles, members)` (pure, the **generic** referential-integrity invariant — a member row naming a role the contract doesn't define; needs no app spec). Exported from `index.ts`. (2) **web10-social** (`data/groups.ts`) — `FOLLOWERS_CONTRACT_SPEC` (`roles: FOLLOWER_ROLES`, `join_policy: 'open'`, `tags: [followers]`, **no `members`** — the `anyone` row is the owner's choice) + `ensureFollowers` now calls `reconcileGroupContract` (fire-and-forget, non-blocking, non-fatal) instead of the old clobbering `anyone` re-heal — which is **removed**. (3) **authenticator** (`ui/.../Groups/ContractHealth.tsx`) — the "check every contract, if not equal, surface it" surface: a "Check health" action in the Groups/Manage tab runs `findDanglingGrants` across the user's managed groups (the generic invariant — the authenticator is D60, it doesn't know web10-social's spec) and surfaces drift ("N groups have grants that do nothing — the app that owns each group repairs it on your next sign-in"). **Tests:** SDK `v3.test.ts` +14 (diff: missing role / permission gap / missing member / join-policy drift / missing tags / in-sync no-op; merge: appends missing roles verbatim + unions a missing op without dropping others + no input mutation; reconcile: no-op in sync / heals the missing `reader` role with the full merged list / unions a missing op / adds a missing member / appends missing tags preserving the owner's / resets a drifted join policy / never touches what the spec doesn't declare; findDanglingGrants: the `reader` bug / clean / empty role / undefined). web10-social `follows.test.ts` re-pinned +1 (ensureFollowers delegates to reconcileGroupContract with the followers spec — roles include `reader`, `members` is undefined; the `anyone` row is never re-added; a heal failure is non-fatal). ui `contractHealth.test.tsx` +4 (idle affordance / all-healthy / surfaces a dangling grant naming the group + grant + repair pointer / a group that fails to read is skipped). 152 sdk + 997 web10-social + 168 ui green, all `tsc --noEmit` clean, sdk dist rebuilt. **The failure-mode scrutiny (17 modes, in the KB):** the two that would have been bugs if unhandled — clobbering a user choice (#2) and sending a role delta instead of the full merged list (#17) — are the ones the scrutiny exists to catch; the rest (concurrent heals converge via ReplacingMergeTree dedup, truncated member lists only cause benign duplicates, owner-added roles/tags are never touched, an owner-deleted app-required role is re-guaranteed by the app on next sign-in, etc.) are documented with their safe behavior.

fix(shared) + test(web10-social) + docs(kb): **the hover preview's duration badge is a live time-lapse (the elapsed clock, not a frozen length)** — operator pass (28.09.2026, a hover-preview screenshot of a Home tile playing): "video plays great in the youtube home view but time lapsed in the video doesnt update, stuck at the length of the video throught the whole thing". **The root (one shared component, both apps — `@web10/discover`):** the `HomeCard`'s bottom-right badge was a **static total** (`formatDuration(media.duration_seconds)`), so it sat frozen at the clip's length (e.g. "2:03") the whole time the preview played — the operator wanted it to be a live time-lapse (the elapsed position counting up), like the YouTube home. **The fix:** `HoverVideo` surfaces the preview's live position to its parent via two new optional callbacks — `onTime(current, duration)` (fired from the `timeupdate` / `loadedmetadata` / `durationchange` listeners, reporting the element's raw values since the React state updates are async) and `onPlayingChange(playing)` (fired from the `playing` / `pause` listeners); the callbacks are kept in refs so the empty-deps listener effect always calls the latest closure without re-binding. `HomeCard` lifts that into `liveCurrent` + `previewPlaying` and the badge becomes a **time-lapse**: at rest it shows the clip's total length, while the preview plays it counts up the **elapsed** position (the YouTube home behavior — the badge is a live clock, not a frozen length), and it returns to the total when the pointer leaves (the `pause` signal). **Tests:** new `homeCard.test.tsx` +3 (at rest the badge is the total — 123s → "2:03"; while the preview plays the badge counts up the elapsed position — "0:30" then "1:02" as `timeupdate` fires; on leave it returns to the total). 996 web10-social + 277 marketing-ui green, `tsc --noEmit` clean. KB: `video-player.md` "The hover preview" + `discover-card.md` item 1 (the badge is a live time-lapse, not a static length).

Both are now `absolute inset-0` (the poster is the backdrop, the video overlays it and fades in on `playing`) — the same box, stacked, never flowed. (2) **the progress bar was decorative** — it was `pointer-events-none` (the `<a>` owned the click), so clicking a spot on the bar did nothing. (i.e. don't bake an app's social signal into the node). **(1) The "It's quiet here" root cause (the real one):** the D0 people directory (`POST /v3/users/directory` → `list_public_users`, `api/app/v3/services/clickhouse.py`) only listed users who had a readable `profile` **face** doc in their followers group — a user with no face was *absent*. `ensureProfile()` (3.153.0) seeds a face on sign-in, but only for users who sign in *after* it shipped, so a node's pre-existing users (and test users) had no face → the directory read empty → "It's quiet here" despite 54 users. One `getGroupMembers` per card, bounded by the page size; anon / no-follows → 0. The node returns only the universal primitives (user, unspoofable follower count, profile face) — it never computes an app's social signal, so a notes/music/shop app can use the same directory without the node knowing "mutuals". (This reverses the first cut, which baked `_reader_following_set` + `_mutual_counts` into the node — the D60 smell the operator flagged.) **(3) The "easy filters" (the operator's "some easy filters for that kind of stuff"):** the Explore tab's People section gains a **People filter chip row** (`?personFilter=`, deep-linkable): **All** (the bare URL — the public directory) | **Following** (the people you follow) | **Mutuals** (the directory filtered to mutuals > 0) | **Followers** (the people who follow you). Following/Followers are the reader's own graph (the directory can't express them) → new `fetchMyFollowingCards()` (`byUserGroups`-backed, the D80 M1 read) + `fetchMyFollowersCards()` (`getGroupMembers` on your own followers group), face-enriched, cached once loaded; Mutuals reuses the directory. The Groups section gains a **Groups filter chip row** (`?groupFilter=`): **All** (the bare URL — the public directory) | **My Groups** (the groups you're a member of, `getMyCommunityGroups` + `MyGroupRow` + Leave) | **Discover** (the public directory — the explicit "find new groups" framing). (3) **logistics** — the count is the number of `repost_of` posts (one per reposter, self-healing: delete your repost post and the tally drops) and is stable across refresh (a read of post docs, not a reaction flip); a repost is a real post in the reposter's followers group so it resurfaces in their feed as a "reposted" card. **Surfaces:** `PostLightbox` / `ProfileFeed` / `DiscoverScreen` / `GroupDetailScreen` all drop `toggleRepost` + the optimistic reaction toggle, wire `onToggleRepost` → `setRepostingTo` (via `useRepost`), and re-derive the count + fill from the post-based reads. **Tests:** `repostSurfaces.test.tsx` (new, 8 — the repeat icon opens the composer in repost mode on all four surfaces + the count is `repost_of` posts + the fill is the reader's own repost post), `data/posts.test.ts` +6 (`readRepostCounts` I3-scoped `count(DISTINCT doc_id)` + degrade-to-empty + no-ids no-op; `readMyRepostedIds` own-followers-group read + username match + signed-out). 930 web10-social green, `tsc --noEmit` clean. **KB:** `social/reposts.md` — the "unify the other surfaces" follow-up is closed (the repeat icon is unified onto the post model on every surface; the count is `repost_of` posts on every surface; the legacy reaction is a read-only fill fallback). The group contract gains **`membership_visibility`** (`public` | `hidden`, sibling of `join_policy` + `discoverable`); a membership row `(G, M)` is publicly enumerable **iff `G.membership_visibility == public`** — one rule, every read surface. web10-social sets it per group type at creation (followers/community = `public`, dm/close-friends = `hidden`). The social graph (who follows whom) is public (the thesis — "your number here is real", "a real network, not a dark forest"); DM relationships are private (DM groups are `hidden`). **The read surfaces:** (1) `POST /v3/groups/by-user` — "what groups is X in?" (public-visibility only, optional `tag` filter, paged, anon-readable, returns group metadata); (2) the `memberships` query-engine CTE (opt-in, read-only view over `group_members`, same category as `group_meta`); (3) `members/list` re-gated on the field. **The IA fixed point (the anti-limbo rule, locked this pass):** the social graph is a property of a *person* → it lives on the *profile* (clickable follower/following counts → dedicated list screens → back to profile), **never** on a discovery surface; **Discover** = pure discovery (Posts | People | Groups); **Groups** nav tab = your communities (restored). **Rejects** (recorded with reasons): global "memberships totally public" (leaks DMs), a per-user `memberships_visible` flag (four-clause rule + reserved node-written service), doc-as-membership (copies the fact out of `group_members`, reserves a writable service name), a `listMembers` D58 op (unnecessary once visibility is a contract field). **Lane scoped** in `knowledge/strategy/parallel-execution.md` — `membership-visibility (D80)`, M0–M7 (M0 the field → M1 `by-user` / M2 the CTE / M3 `members/list` gate → M4 the profile list screens → M5 the Discover People cleanup → M6 the Explorer→Discover rename + Groups nav restore → M7 the screenshot pass). No code change this entry — decision + plan only.

test(e2e) + fix(web10-social) + docs(kb): **the two-user notifications gauntlet — and the real bug it caught: the reaction/comment nudges targeted a non-existent peer, so real-time notifications never fired** — operator: "do the gauntlets, then we can do the fixes! let's follow the ai use theory." **The gauntlet (`e2e/tests/social-notifications.spec.ts`, new):** the notifications version of social-p2p.spec.ts (which covers the DM fast path). Two layers (the test ladder): (1) **API floor** — the data-integrity of the read-side derivation (B's reaction on A's post is a `reactions` doc with `ref_value` = A's post, readable by A — the CRUD read `deriveNotifications` keys off); (2) **browser gauntlet** — the load-bearing witness: B reacts to A's post in the real app → A's `nav-notifications-badge` pops to **1 in real time** (the P2P nudge, no reload on A) → A opens `/notifications` → the history shows "B reacted to your post" → marked read (badge clears). Two separate browser instances + the mDNS flag (same as social-p2p). **The bug it caught (Phase 3 compare → Phase 4 repair):** the gauntlet's first run was RED — A's badge never bumped. The seam logs showed the break: B's `sendP2P` logged `sending to web10/{a}` but A's peer id is `api_localhost {a} web10 web10-social` — a **provider mismatch**. The reaction/comment nudges used `post.author_provider` (the reply nudge, `extractProvider(comment.author_key)`) as the target provider, but v3 `author_key`s are **bare usernames**, so `extractProvider` falls back to the `'web10'` default — a peer id that doesn't exist. The nudge was "queued on open" and the channel never opened (no peer with that id), so the real-time notification silently never landed. The DM nudge was immune — it uses the provider from the conversation key (the node's provider), which is why DMs worked. **The fix:** the write side now targets `token.provider` (the actor's provider = the node's provider, since v3 is same-node) instead of the derived `author_provider` — `reactions.ts` (the reaction nudge) + `comments.ts` (the reply + comment nudges; the now-unused `extractProvider` import dropped). The follow nudge was already correct (defaults to `token.provider`). **Verified:** the gauntlet is green (the logs now show B sending to `api.localhost/{a}`, A receiving `inbound … {"type":"reaction"}`, the store `nudge — appended … unread: 1`, and `markAllRead — all read, unread: 0`); 891 web10-social tests green, `tsc` clean. **Shard:** added to `global-config` (next to social-p2p). **KB:** `web10-social-v3/notifications.md` documents the provider gotcha (target = the node's provider, never the derived `author_provider`). **Open:** the presence dot + the real-time-off (CRUD-only) forks remain the messages gauntlet's territory; `getPendingRequests` (request-join groups) is still unbuilt but not needed for follows.

feat(api) + test(api) + docs(kb): **the query engine reads group metadata — a new opt-in `group_meta` boundary CTE (QE-A, the keystone node change)** — the D73 safe-query engine now exposes group metadata (`member_count` from `group_members`, `join_policy` + `discoverable` from `group_contracts`) through a second API-built boundary CTE, so a caller's query can `JOIN group_meta gm ON p.group_id = gm.group_id` and sort by legit audience size. **The security model (the wall extends, it doesn't weaken):** `group_meta` is opt-in (`withGroupMeta: true` on `POST /v3/query`; without it, `group_meta` is an unknown table and the query 403s). The raw tables (`group_members`, `group_contracts`) stay in `RAW_TABLES` — a direct reference is rejected even with the opt-in on, including inside caller CTEs / subqueries (the AST walk + re-parse backstop are unchanged in structure). **Visibility = the existing I3 gate, NULL-out-and-sort-last:** the endpoint computes the reader's readable set (union of `readable_groups` over the services the query touches; for a standalone `group_meta` query, the reader's own memberships among the candidates) and passes it to `_group_meta_cte_sql(readable, candidates)`. The CTE **full-scans all candidate groups** and CASE-NULLs the metadata of the unreadable ones — it must NOT copy the service CTE's `WHERE group_id IN (readable)` filter (that would silently drop unreadable groups and break the honest "there are groups I can't read" signal). Unreadable groups are present as NULLs, so `ORDER BY member_count` is I3-honest: they sort to the bottom and reveal nothing beyond their existence. The per-row check is a set-membership test on a precomputed set (vectorizes), not a correlated function. **The build:** (1) `_group_meta_cte_sql` (`safe_query.py`) — pre-aggregated active member counts (same shape as `_get_group_member_counts`, dedup-then-filter tombstone invariant) LEFT JOINed to the deduped `group_contracts` (latest row, not-deleted) for `join_policy` + `discoverable`, filtered to the candidates, with CASE-based NULLing on the readable set; edge shapes are shape-valid + ClickHouse 24.8-safe (no candidates → `WHERE 1 = 0` empty CTE; no readable → plain `CAST(NULL AS …)` columns; `Nullable` casts required — 24.8 rejects `CAST(NULL AS String)` with CANNOT_CONVERT_TYPE). (2) `_validate` / `query_services` / `build_safe_query` gain the opt-in: `group_meta` is recognized as an API-built CTE (not a service) when on, excluded from the service set, and injected only if the query references it. (3) `QueryRequest` gains `withGroupMeta: bool = False`; the endpoint computes the readable set (parallel to `readable_groups_by_service`) and threads it to the compiler; the log line records the flag. **Tests:** `test_safe_query.py` +11 (opt-in gate, CTE injection, CASE-NULL-not-WHERE-filter, raw tables still blocked with the flag on, raw table in a caller CTE still caught, the content-join reference shape compiles + re-parses, no-inject-when-unreferenced, both edge shapes, `query_services` excludes `group_meta`); `test_query_endpoint.py` +4 (standalone injects + serializes, no-flag 403, the join passes the readable set, raw table 403 with the flag on). 988 api tests green, `ruff` clean (check + format). **KB:** `safe-query.md` (the `group_meta` CTE section + the walk step + the pinned-test table + the wiring) + `query-engine.md` (the Group metadata section). **Open:** QE-B (the SDK `withGroupMeta`), QE-C (the I3 anti-test seatbelt), QE-D (the D0/D3 migration, gated on A/B/C); the QE-7 detail-endpoint tightening (metadata iff you can read the group) is decided but not yet implemented.

Decision 2: **one edit model, atomic commit** — edit mode stages face + settings; Save/Publish commits them together in one ordered sequence (the "atomic go"); the live state is frozen at the last commit. **Built (data layer, `src/data/groups.ts`):** (1) **`GroupIdentity` (the D60 face) gains `status?: 'draft'|'published'`** (absent = `published`, so every pre-existing group is live) **and the staging-setting fields** — `visibility` (who-can-read), `join_policy` (how-join), `discoverable` (list-in-directory) — staged in the face during edit and applied to the contract only at commit; `writeGroupIdentity` persists them. feat(api) + feat(sdk) + feat(web10-social) + test + docs(kb): **groups carry a platform-level `tags` column — web10-social classifies its groups by tag (D78)** — operator, after the "followers groups showing in My Groups" bug: "is this a fundamental protocol flaw? should groups themselves have tags? … this would be an issue for any app architecture not just social media. we could add tags to the groups in clickhouse, make a clickhouse upgrade right?" Tag scheme: `web10-social-group` / `web10-social-followers` / `web10-social-dm` (+ `web10-social-chat`). **The model (KB-first, `groups/overview.md` "Group Tags" + D78):** `group_contracts` gains a **`tags` column** (`Array(String)`, default `[]`) — the group-primitive analog of `documents.tags`. The platform stores + matches them (`has(tags, …)`); the app decides what they mean. It is the group-side of the existing doc-tag primitive: both primitives carry generic string labels, the platform filters on them, the app assigns meaning. The `discoverable` flag is the precedent (a platform-level group attribute added via `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`). **Why it beats the id-pattern blocklist.** My Groups was a client-side blocklist of id shapes (`/followers`, `dm-`, `-{username}`, exact discover) — brittle: it leaked followed users' followers groups (the reported bug) and group chats (a known v1 gap), and any new infra group type leaks. A tag **whitelist** inverts it: a group shows in a surface only if it carries that surface's tag; infra groups are excluded by construction; a new group type just gets a new tag; selection is one server-side read, I3-scoped. **Built.** (1) **ClickHouse** — `group_contracts.tags` column (boot ALTER); `create_group`/`update_group`/`get_group` carry tags; `get_user_groups(member, tags)` adds the server-side `has(gc.tags, %(tagN)s)` filter. (2) **API** — `CreateGroup`/`UpdateGroup`/`ListMyGroups` models + the `/create`/`/update`/`/list` endpoints wire tags. (3) **SDK** — `V3Group.tags`; `createGroup`/`updateGroup`/`getMyGroups({ tags })`. (4) **web10-social** — `GROUP_TAG` constants; tag at creation (`ensureFollowers`→`-followers`, `ensureDmGroup`→`-dm`, `createCommunityGroup`→`-group`, `createGroupChat`→`-chat`); `getMyCommunityGroups` = `getMyGroups({ tags: ['web10-social-group'] })`, `getMyGroupChats` = `getMyGroups({ tags: ['web10-social-chat'] })` — both now server-side tag reads, no client-side pattern matching (supersedes the 3.115.1 `isFollowersGroup` fix for the Groups surface; that fix stays for `people.ts`). (5) **Migration** — one-time, sentinel-gated `_migrate_group_tags_backfill` seeds legacy (untagged) groups from their id shape; the tag is authoritative after it runs. **Relationship to the face `kind` (D77).** The group **tag** is the *selection* classifier (which surface); the face **`kind`** is a *render* hint; the tag supersedes `kind` for surface routing, `kind` is retained for backward compat + render. **Tests.** API: `create_group`/`update_group` with tags, `get_user_groups` tag filter (`has` clause), the migration (`_infer_group_tag` + backfill seeds-untagged-only + sentinel skip) — 961 green. SDK: `createGroup`/`getMyGroups({tags})`/`updateGroup` tag threading — 125 green. web10-social: `getMyCommunityGroups` + `getMyGroupChats` select by tag, create functions tag correctly — 818 green, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

fix(web10-social) + test(web10-social) + docs(kb): **Shorts on mobile no longer has the bottom tab bar blocking the like/comment/share rail + the comment input — the lens is full-bleed with a back arrow to get out** — operator (two screenshots, `/shorts` on a phone): "on mobile, the bottom bar is blocking both adding a comment and share button" + "when you open comments it should hide the shorts bar always." **The root (z-index + geometry, not a missing toggle):** the mobile bottom nav (`Layout.tsx`, `fixed bottom-0 inset-x-0 z-20`, ~58px) always renders below `md`, and it painted over the shorts action rail (`ShortsScreen.tsx`, `absolute bottom-6 right-3`, z-auto) and the comment sheet (`absolute inset-x-0 bottom-0 z-10`) — both anchored to the slide's bottom edge, which on a phone (mobile browser chrome / `100vh` vs visual-viewport) lands inside the nav band. The content wrapper's `pb-16` reserve was meant to keep content clear of the fixed nav, but the shorts viewport is `h-full` and the reserve didn't reliably hold on a real device, so the rail + the comment input (the last element of the sheet's scroll area) sat behind the `z-20` bar. **The fix (the TikTok model — the lens is immersive, the bar is gone on it):** (1) `Layout.tsx` gains `isShorts = pathname.startsWith('/shorts')` — on the lens the bottom nav is `hidden` and the wrapper drops its `pb-16` (so the video runs edge-to-edge, truly full-bleed, no dead band). The mobile top header stays (account actions remain reachable); the exit is the back arrow below. (2) `ShortsScreen.tsx` renders a **back arrow** top-left over the video (`data-testid="shorts-back"`, `aria-label="Back to feed"`, `ChevronLeft`, a `sticky top-4 left-4 z-30` pill so it stays pinned while you swipe) → `navigate('/feed')` (the home base — the operator's call: feed, not discover). **The children-indexing gotcha (the real fix behind the fix):** the back button is a child of the swipe container, and three code paths indexed the slides by `container.children` position — the keyboard swipe (`handleKeyDown`), the active-slide `IntersectionObserver`, and the deep-link scroll. The button shifted every index by one (the first "slide" became the button), which broke the keyboard swipe + the ambient-autoplay handover (the active index never matched a real slide). A `slideEls()` helper (the container's `[data-testid^="short-slide-"]` children, in order) now backs all three, so the slides are addressed by slide, never by raw child position. **Harness:** `screenshots/harness/mock-data.ts` was missing the `uploadCommentPhoto` stub (3.113.0's photos-in-comments added it to the `@/data` barrel but not the mock) — the real `CommentThread` the shorts lens mounts imports it, so the capture errored `No matching export`; stub added (returns a fake doc_id + url, degrades offline). **Tests:** `shortsScreen.test.tsx` +1 (the back arrow renders labelled + carries the chevron, and tapping it navigates `/shorts` → `/feed` via a route probe). 820 web10-social tests green, `tsc --noEmit` clean. **Verified (Playwright geometry probe, 375px):** the bottom nav is not visible on `/shorts`; the back button sits top-left over the video (x≈16, below the header); the video runs to the full viewport bottom (the `pb-16` drop made the lens full-bleed); the action rail (like/share) and the comment sheet + input are all fully on-screen — nothing blocked. **KB:** `shorts.md` gains the mobile-lens nav spec (the bar is hidden on the lens, the back arrow is the exit → `/feed`, the `slideEls()` invariant).

3.115.1 || 18.09.2026
fix(web10-social) + test(web10-social): **the notification badge + banner clear when you actually view them — the "viewed but still says new" bug** — operator (screenshot, on Groups with the "2" badge + "2 new notifications" banner still lit): "i have viewed my new notifications and the thing that says they are new hasnt updated, it hasnt changed that i viewed them." **The root (a mark-read race):** `NotificationsScreen` fired `markAllRead()` **once** on mount (`useEffect` with `[]` deps), but `initNotifications()` → `seed()` is async (it derives from ~7+ CRUD reads — my posts, reactions, comments, the all-comments read, the conversation list + last-DM per conversation, the followers member list). If you opened `/notifications` while the seed was still in flight, `items` was empty → `markAllRead()` no-opped (`items.every(read)` is `true` on `[]`) → the `last_seen` cursor never advanced. When the seed then landed the derived rows as unread, `markAllRead` never re-fired (the effect had already run) → the badge + banner stayed at "2" even though you'd looked at them. **The fix (mark-read reacts to `unread`, not just mount):** the screen's effect is now `useEffect(() => { if (unread > 0) markAllRead(); }, [unread])` — it re-runs the moment the seed (or a new nudge) bumps the unread count, so the badge clears the instant the items you're looking at land. `markAllRead` is a no-op when everything is already read, so this never loops; a new nudge while you're sitting on the page is also marked read (you're looking at it). **Tests:** `notifications.test.tsx` — the `useNotifications` mock now re-renders on a controllable emit (so a test can land the seed after mount) + a new regression test "re-marks read when the seed lands after the screen opened (the race)" (asserts the screen does NOT mark an empty store on open, then re-marks when the seed lands; verified to fail against the old one-shot code). 819 web10-social tests green, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

feat(api) + feat(sdk) + feat(shared) + feat(web10-social) + test(both) + docs(kb): **comments page the Facebook way — `ref_value` is the parent, cursor paging at both levels, "view more comments" / "view more replies"** — operator, after the 3.106.0 thread: "is this the right design though? if there are 10000 comments? will need to page" → "what would facebook do" → "do it right here, how facebook would do it!" **The reframe (the 3.106.0 single-read design breaks at 10k):** a hot post has thousands of comments; you can't read them all in one call. The thread must **page**, and paging needs the server to pull "page N of X" for two X's — the post's top-level comments, and one comment's replies. `ref_value` is the column the server filters on, so it must point at the thing being paged. **The model change (KB-first, `social/comments.md` rewritten to the Facebook shape):** a comment's `ref_value` is now its **PARENT** — the post for a top-level comment, the parent comment for a reply (was: always the post). That makes each level an independent server page. The cost: the post's TOTAL comment count is no longer one `GROUP BY ref_value` (replies don't ref the post) — the top-level count stays exact + cheap; the total is top-level + summed reply counts, or a maintained counter at scale (the count is decoupled from the read, the invariant that matters). **Built:** (1) **node** (`clickhouse.py` `read_docs_by_ref`) — keyset cursor paging: `ORDER BY created_at` (tie-broken by `doc_id`) + a `cursor` ("created_at|doc_id" of the previous page's last row) → the next page after the cursor; `ReadDocuments` gains `cursor` + `order` (`asc`/`desc`); the safe-query engine already passes `ORDER BY`/the keyset WHERE through (it re-emits the caller query verbatim). (2) **SDK** — `read()` gains `cursor` + `order` opts (threaded to the payload). (3) **data layer** (`src/data/comments.ts`) — `readComments`/`readReplies` now return a `CommentPage` (`{ comments, nextCursor }`); `readReplies` keys on the parent comment (the "view more replies" page); new `countRepliesByComment` (one `GROUP BY ref_value` over a set of comment ids); `countComments` → top-level count via `readRefCounts`; `createComment` writes `ref_value = parent_id` for a reply (was the post); new thread seams `readThreadComments` (page + likeCount/likedByMe + replyCounts) + `readThreadReplies` (page). (4) **shared thread** (`marketing/shared/discover/src/CommentThread.tsx`) — rewritten to the paged model: opens with the first top-level page, pre-fetches each comment's first reply page (bounded + parallel, driven by `replyCounts`), and renders the two hyperlink-style pagers — **"View more comments"** (next top-level page) + **"View more replies"** (next reply page for that comment). The seam is paged (`ReadComments`/`ReadReplies` return `CommentPageResult`); the marketing public-ledger reader returns the whole flat conversation as one page (no `replyCounts`) and the thread builds the tree by grouping on `parent_id` (both apps, one component). docs(strategy): **D76 — node licensing is SSPL-1.0, free core, no gate: the "next WordPress" model** — operator, after the Gumroad-license-key thread: "i get it so no gumroad! just sspl it! no gating it!" **The decision:** the node is SSPL-1.0 (the `LICENSE`, verbatim SSPL v1); the core is free to run / self-host / extend — **no license key, no tier gate, no registration cap, no "you need a license" pester.** Monetization is on the *service*, not the software (D57): hosted nodes (usage tiers), node ads (10–15% take), the no-ads subscription (70/30), enterprise ($999+, SLA/DR/white-glove). The personal/influencer/corporate tiers are **hosting + service tiers, not software licenses** (personal = free core, influencer = hosted node, corporate = enterprise/VIP — the WordPress core / .com / VIP mapping). **Why SSPL:** a license key / usage gate on the core is the one thing that kills the "next WordPress" play (WordPress core is free for commercial use — no key, no cap — and that is *why* it won; MongoDB/Elastic license moves are the cautionary tales). SSPL §13 is the moat around the actual revenue line (hosted nodes = web10-as-a-service): offer a *modified* web10 as a service → release the Service Source Code — it stops closed-source service clones, the AWS-DynamoDB-vs-MongoDB dynamic. MIT is rejected (no service-layer moat; a competitor could close-source and resell). **The soft wall, done right:** no "you need a license" banner (it sours the no-landlord brand); the nudge is an *upsell to a service*, not a demand for compliance ("your node's getting poppin — want us to host it?"); no registration cap on the free core (a big self-hosted node is a *lighthouse*, not a free-rider to cap). **The line:** the landlord owns the *building service*, never the *software*. **Honest costs:** SSPL is source-available, not OSI open source (small halo loss, accepted); the **SDK-embedding gray area** (§13 scope when web10's data layer is embedded in a third party's closed product) is flagged for a lawyer's read *before* it matters, not assumed. **Rejects:** the Gumroad key, the usage/registration cap, the pester banner, rebranding the SSPL text (the 3.99.1 fix), and MIT. Docs only (decision record); the `licensing.md` KB spec is the open follow-up.
