The license text is a creative work copyrighted by MongoDB; rebranding the name does not transfer that copyright, so the "web10" line was a legal nullity that undermined the exact Section-13 (network-use) protection it was meant to provide. **The fix (use the license, don't rewrite it):** (1) restore line 4 to `Copyright © 2018 MongoDB, Inc.` — the copyright in the *license text*, kept verbatim as the SSPL requires; web10's copyright is asserted on the web10 source code, not on the license document; (2) `git mv LICENSE-Community.txt LICENSE` (the "Community" suffix implied the old MongoDB Community Source License, which this is not); (3) a README **License** section stating the posture in plain terms — run/self-host/build free, the one Section-13 condition (offer a *modified* web10 as a service → release the Service Source Code), why the MongoDB copyright line is intentional, and that SSPL is source-available (not OSI open source). No code change. The licensing *strategy* (free core, value in hosting + node ads + enterprise, the "soft wall" as a hosted-upgrade nudge rather than a license gate) is the open thread from this discussion — to be filed as a decision + KB doc when scoped.

fix(api) + fix(web10-social) + fix(e2e) + test(e2e) + docs(kb): **the D73 feed query actually renders — ClickHouse was qualifying the result column names and the row→client contract was silently breaking** — CI (e2e shard 2/4 + 4/4) caught what the unit tests can't: the mocked `w.query` never ran the feed SQL against a real ClickHouse, so the column-name mangling shipped green. **The root (a ClickHouse column-naming rule, not a bug in the engine):** ClickHouse names a result column after the *qualified* expression (`p.body`) whenever **any other table in the join scope exposes a same-named column** — the feed's count subqueries expose `ref_value`, the JOINed profile subquery exposes `author_key` + `body`. So the row keys arrived as `p.author_key` / `p.body` / `p.ref_value` (while `doc_id` / `tags` / `created_at` stayed clean — the *partial* mangling is what made it silent: no error anywhere, the feed just rendered empty). The prepare pass made it worse: `resolve_media_urls_in_docs` reads `doc.get("body", {})` → `{}` (the key is `p.body`) → media never resolved, and it wrote back a phantom `body: {}`. The client's `fromFeedQueryRow` read `row.body` → the phantom → posts with no text, no media, no author. **The fix (the row keys are the contract — pin them):** (1) **the feed query aliases every selected column** (`p.body AS body`, `p.author_key AS author_key`, …) so the result names are stable regardless of join scope (`src/data/feed.ts` `buildFeedQuery`); (2) **the endpoint logs the contract** — `[query] … compiled=<sql>` before execution and `[query] … rows=N columns=[…]` after (`api/app/v3/endpoints/query.py`), so a mangled contract is visible at the source, not as an empty feed downstream (the logging that was missing when this bug took 40 min to find locally); (3) **the e2e contract** — `social-groups.spec.ts` granted only `posts`, but the D73 feed query references `posts` + `reactions` + `comments` + `profile`, so the app-contract gate 403'd the whole query (a posts-only contract can't load the feed); it now grants the full set like the other feed-exercising specs. **The seam test the unit tests can't provide:** `query-engine.spec.ts` +1 — the feed shape (qualified SELECT + JOINed same-named columns) must return *unqualified* keys (`body` / `author_key` / `ref_value`, no `p.*`), run against a real ClickHouse. **KB:** `query-engine.md` gains "The column-name contract (alias every selected column)" — the rule + why the failure is partial and silent; the SDK's `w.query()` JSDoc carries the same rule for app developers. 6 e2e failures (3 social-feed browser gauntlets + node-ads + social-groups + ads) → the 5 deterministic ones green; the ads-picker one is a pre-existing eventual-consistency flake under parallel load (passes in isolation, passes on `origin/dev`, this PR touches no ad-path code).

So "mine" was **never found**: every heart tap fell through to the create branch, stacking a fresh reaction doc per tap (28 taps → 28 docs → the count read 28), and the same compare left the lightbox + group-detail heart **un-filled on a post the user had already liked** (their initial-state loads had the identical compare). **The fix (the v3 ownership rule, username alone):** the "mine" match in `setReaction` + `toggleReactionKind` drops the provider compare (`r.author_username === token.username`); the same fix lands in the two initial-state loads (`PostLightbox.tsx`, `GroupDetailScreen.tsx`). fix(web10-social) + test(web10-social): **trending video posts stop rendering other posts' media — the "blacked out" tile** — operator: "on the trending tab, a posted video is blacked out dont know why, greyed out." **The root (an aliasing mutation in `DiscoverScreen.loadDiscover`):** the per-author media grouping built its ref accumulator as `refs: p.media_refs || []` — a **reference to the first post's own `media_refs` array** — and then `entry.refs.push(...)` for every later post by the same author, mutating that first post's array in place. The per-post filter that follows (`media.filter(m => postRefIds.has(m._id))`, built from the same now-polluted `p.media_refs`) then matched **all of the author's media against the first post**: a single-video post rendered a `MediaCarousel` of every other post's media by that author. The blackout itself: the carousel hardcodes video slides to the **raw source file** (`MediaCarousel.tsx` `type: 'file'`), and for a transcoded (D44) upload that source is the original camera file — typically HEVC/AV1, which Chromium cannot decode → a black, greyed-out tile (no poster, no playable first frame). It only bit when one author had **two or more media posts on the board** (your video + any other post of yours), which is why the feed (no per-author grouping) and single-post boards looked fine. **The fix:** copy the array when creating the author entry (`refs: [...(p.media_refs || [])]`) — the accumulator is now its own array, the posts' `media_refs` are never mutated, and the per-post filter matches only the post's own refs. **Test:** `discoverScreen.test.tsx` +1 regression (same author, a video post + an image post: the video post renders its own single inline video with **no carousel**, the image post renders its own image, and the first post's `media_refs` array is unmutated) — verified to fail on the pre-fix code. 497 web10-social tests green, `tsc --noEmit` clean. `screenshots/discover-{desktop,375}.png` + `discover-youtube-{desktop,375}.png` re-captured (the harness seed — nova with a single-ref post + a 3-ref post — is exactly the bug scenario; the old shot shows the leaked `1/3` carousel on the single-ref card).

It reads the post by `doc_id` (`get_document_any_author` — the URL's `post_id`; the `username` is the display author for the canonical URL, not the read key, so a reshared link still resolves), reads its groups, and decides **public-readability** via the D58 read gate (`can_read_group(group, "anon", "posts", authenticated=False)` on any of the post's groups). The rule: **no surface owns a `<video>`; every surface composes `<VideoPlayer>`.** The inline tap-to-play now lives once in `InlineVideo`, and the invariant is a property of the component: **a tap toggles play/pause in place and `stopPropagation`s — it never reaches the card.** `hls` delegates to the existing `HlsVideoPlayer` (kept as-is — it is the `hls` source renderer, and it's unit-tested standalone); `youtube` is a wired-but-unused source case (an `<iframe>` — the Shorts path, a source case not a component). **The two modalities (where, not how):** *inline* = a stream (Feed, Discover, Groups) — video plays in place, comments expand in-card; *modal* = a gallery (Profile grid → lightbox, deep-link) — a static poster cell, tap → `PostLightbox` (`mode="full"`). Orthogonal, they compose. **Migrations:** Feed `MediaItem` → `<VideoPlayer>` (transcoded → `hls`/full, non-transcoded → `file`/inline, `media-video` testid preserved); Discover grid `MediaVideo` → `<VideoPlayer fit=cover ratio=16/9>` + the comment count is now a button that toggles an inline `CommentThread` (the feed's pattern) + the `PostLightbox` is **removed from Discover** (no `lightboxPost` state, no `flatMediaMap`); Discover YouTube view → web10 video posts render inline in the 16:9 tile (the TikTok/Shorts wall, no lightbox); Groups `PostMedia` → `<VideoPlayer mode=inline>`; `PostLightbox`'s `LightboxVideo` → `<VideoPlayer mode=full>`. **Tests:** new `videoPlayer.test.tsx` (7: source routing hls→rack / file→inline / file+full→native controls / youtube→iframe, the 16:9 cover tile, `sourceFromMedia` transcoded→hls vs raw→file, and the stopPropagation invariant — the actual bug); the two Discover "card opens the lightbox" tests re-pinned to the new intent (card click opens **no** lightbox; the comment count toggles the inline thread; the YouTube card renders the video inline). Screenshot harness gains a `discover-youtube` screen. 478 web10-social tests green, `tsc --noEmit` clean. **Still open (in the KB):** multi-media posts (the feed's `MediaGrid` shows only item 1 — needs an inline carousel) and real YouTube embeds (a data-model question before a rendering one).

(screenshot: the Ad Inventory card's error state — "Couldn't load your node ads / No app contract for https://auth.web10.app to readAll on posts"). **The root:** the authenticator (`ui/`) is the node's first-party console AND a CRUD client — the Studio's ad surfaces (`AdsCard`, `AdInventoryCard`) read/write `posts` docs (the creator's catalog + the node's inventory), and `DirectDealsCard` writes `ads`. Those calls carry `Origin: <auth origin>`, and the documents endpoint enforces an app contract per origin+service+operation (`documents.py _check_app_permission`). Third-party apps get their contract via the consent popup, but the authenticator can't open a popup to itself — it IS the consent UI — and nothing ever granted it a contract for its own origin. So every Studio ad read/create/update/delete 403'd with "No app contract for https://auth.web10.app to readAll on posts". The e2e gauntlet masked it: `node-ads.spec.ts` manually seeds a contract for the AUTH origin before driving the card, so the test passed while the real console was broken. **The fix (`ui/src/interfaces/Interface.tsx`):** on sign-in (both an explicit login and a cookie session restore — `servicesLoad` is the shared hook for both) the authenticator grants itself an app contract for `window.location.origin` covering the services its own CRUD touches (`posts`, `ads`) × the four document operations (`create`, `readAll`, `updateOwn`, `deleteOwn`). It is the only origin allowed to call `app-contracts/add` (authenticator-origin-gated), so it is architecturally the right party to self-grant; the grant is per-user (user_key), idempotent (`add_app_contract` upserts; skipped when the loaded contract list already covers the origin), and best-effort (a failure is logged, never thrown — sign-in must not break). **Tests:** `selfContract.test.tsx` (4 — the grant fires for the auth origin with the ad services + the user's token; it is idempotent (skips when already granted); a grant failure is swallowed, never thrown; `servicesLoad` triggers it on sign-in). 233 ui tests green, `tsc -b` clean. The e2e's manual AUTH-origin seed is now redundant (a harmless upsert) but kept — it still pins the gauntlet's intent.

chore(ci): **the box e2e runner no longer poisons its own checkout — the api container's root-owned artifacts (`.venv`, `__pycache__`, rtc `node_modules`) stay out of the host checkout** — after 3.77.4, the next run died in **5s** with `##[error]File was unable to be removed Error: EACCES: permission denied, unlink '…/api/.venv/.gitignore'`. **The root:** the `api` Dockerfile bakes a root-owned `.venv` at `/web10` (`uv sync`), but the e2e compose bind-mounts `../api:/web10` — which **shadows** the baked venv with the (venv-less) host checkout. So `uv run` recreates `.venv` *in the host checkout*, root-owned (the container runs as root). A re-run then failed on a *different* root-owned file — `api/app/__pycache__/*.pyc` (Python compiles the mounted `app/` in place). The `rtc` service has the identical shape (`bun install` bakes `/rtc/node_modules`; the `../api/rtc:/rtc` mount shadows it). On the **next** run, `actions/checkout`'s workspace cleanup tries to delete those root-owned files as `ci-runner` → EACCES → the whole job fails before a single test runs. **The fix (two parts, mirrors the `ui` service which already does the volume half):** (1) named volumes shadow the deps dirs so the container reuses the image's baked deps — `api-venv:/web10/.venv` + `rtc-node-modules:/rtc/node_modules` (registered in the compose `volumes:` block; the `ui` service's `ui-node-modules:/ui/node_modules` is the precedent); (2) `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: "1"` on the `api` service so Python never writes `__pycache__`/`.pyc` into the mounted source tree (the app writes no other artifacts to CWD — verified). One-time box cleanup: the already-poisoned root-owned files (63) in the runner's `_work` were removed. No product change.

fix(api) + test(api) + chore(deps): **drop passlib, call bcrypt directly — the signup/login time bomb is gone** — the `bcrypt<4.1` cap (the one dependabot PR #759 was deliberately excluded from in 3.70.1) was a load-bearing workaround for a passlib bug, not a bcrypt one. **The real bug:** passlib 1.7.4 (unmaintained since 2020) runs a backend self-test (`detect_wrap_bug`) on first use that feeds a **255-byte** secret to `bcrypt.hashpw` — bcrypt < 4.1 silently truncated it to 72 bytes (self-test passed), bcrypt >= 4.1 raises `ValueError: password cannot be longer than 72 bytes` (self-test blows up during backend init → every signup/login 500s). The `bcrypt.__about__` read the old note blamed is wrapped in a `try/except` and only logs — a red herring. **The fix (`api/app/services/auth.py`):** drop `passlib[bcrypt]` entirely and call `bcrypt` directly — `get_password_hash` → `bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode()[:72], bcrypt.gensalt())`, `verify_password` → `bcrypt.checkpw(...)` (a malformed hash returns `False`, not a raise). The `[:72]` truncation is **exactly correct, not a workaround**: bcrypt's algorithm only ever consumes the first 72 bytes, so this restores the old passlib path's observable behavior and means no caller ever hits the ValueError. **Migration-safe:** pre-existing `$2b$` hashes (the v2→v3 account migration carries `hashed_password` verbatim, no re-hash — plan 3.31.1) still verify unchanged. **Deps (`api/pyproject.toml`):** `passlib[bcrypt]>=1.7` removed, `bcrypt<4.1` cap removed, `bcrypt>=4.1` added (locks to 5.0.0); `uv.lock` re-resolved (bcrypt 4.0.1 → 5.0.0, passlib 1.7.4 dropped). **Tests:** the `pwd_context` mock-based cases in `test_auth_services.py` + `test_main.py` re-pinned to real bcrypt round-trips (hash shape, correct/wrong verify, malformed-hash → `False`, 100-char password truncates to its 72-byte prefix). 959 api tests green, `ruff check` clean. **Supersedes #759** (the `<4.1`→`<5.1` bump is now moot — the cap is gone).

fix(web10-social) + test(web10-social): **DM presence + delivery — both parties showing "Offline" when both are online, and sent messages not arriving instantly.** Operator report (screenshot): the operator and a friend were both in the app looking at their DM, both saw the other as "Offline," and a sent message didn't show up immediately — "makes me doubt they are getting connected, also shouldn't need to send a message to be online." **Root cause:** presence (3.39.0/3.40.0) and the P2P fast path are both *passive* — they activate only on a data-channel exchange (a send or an inbound). A peer is "online" only after you've actually exchanged P2P data with them (60s TTL), and a send is only instant if a channel is already open. Two users who are both in the app but haven't messaged each other never open a channel, so: (1) neither is in the other's `onlinePeers` set → both render "Offline" even though both local peers are open (the "Real-time" chip is green — that's only *your* reachability, it tells the other party nothing); (2) the first `sendP2P` pays the full WebRTC handshake, and if the channel isn't open yet the nudge is queued on `open` — so delivery isn't instant. **The fix (two pieces, both in `src/data/p2p.ts` + `DmsScreen`):** **(1) a presence probe on conversation-open** (`probePresence`) — opening a conversation opens (or reuses) the data channel to the other party: channel open → `markOnline` (green), channel `error` (peer unreachable / not on signaling) or `close` → `markOffline` (gray). The channel handshake IS the presence check — no server-side presence service (still deferred per D66). **(2) a presence heartbeat** (`startHeartbeat`, 25s, started in `initP2P`, stopped in `teardownP2P`) — re-probes every tracked peer (a `peerIdentity` map now stores provider/username per peer id, recovered from the id on inbound via `identityFromPeerId`). Two jobs: it keeps each channel WARM so a send goes out instantly (no handshake on the first message), and it refreshes the TTL so a quiet-but-online peer doesn't flip offline after 60s of silence. This is what makes presence + delivery work *without the other party sending anything*. `DmsScreen`'s inbound handler now also refreshes the conversation list's last-message preview (not just the open conversation), so a message arriving while the list is showing updates the row. **Tests:** 5 new `probePresence` (not-ready no-op; open channel → online; not-yet-open → online on open; channel error → offline; probed close → offline) + the TTL-expiry test re-cut for the heartbeat (a reachable peer stays warm past the TTL; an unreachable one expires via the sweep). 374 web10-social tests green, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

fix(api) + test(api) + docs(kb): **the recovery password-change flake, actually fixed** — the e2e `recovery.spec.ts` "API floor — password-change" test ("new password should work") was red ~100% of the time on an active `dev` (and had been flaking since 3.58.1, which claimed to fix it). **Root cause (reproduced 100% against a live ClickHouse):** the `users` table is `ReplacingMergeTree(updated_at)` and `get_user` dedups via `ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 1` — "always the latest" only holds when the new row's `updated_at` is *strictly* greater. The five users-table mutators (`change_password`, `change_phone`, `set_email`, `verify_phone`, `verify_email`) write via `client.command()` (an `INSERT ... SELECT`) and bound `updated_at` as a **raw datetime object** — but clickhouse-connect's `command()` parameter binding **truncates a bound datetime to second precision**, while `create_user`'s `client.insert()` keeps microseconds. A signup and a password-change in the same second → the microsecond `create_user` row outranks the second-truncated `change_password` row → the read returns the stale row (old hash) → the new password 401s. 3.58.1's "use a Python microsecond clock" fix was ineffective because the `command()` binding silently re-truncated it. **The fix** (`api/app/v3/services/clickhouse.py`): (1) the five mutators now bind `updated_at` as a **string** in the `DateTime64` format (`_ch_ts(_now())` — `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff`), the same way every other table already writes it, so sub-second ordering survives; (2) `_now()` now returns a **timezone-aware** UTC datetime (`datetime.now(UTC)`) — a naive datetime is ambiguous: `client.insert()` treats it as process-local and double-shifts it on any non-UTC host, while `client.command()` treats it as UTC (a latent 4h-off bug on west-of-UTC hosts, now closed). **Repro:** a standalone loop driving the exact `complete`-endpoint sequence (`create_user` → `change_password` → `verify_phone` → `get_user`) against a live ClickHouse failed 200/200 before, 0/300 after. **Tests:** `test_v3_clickhouse.py` +5 (`TestUsersMutatorTimestampShape` — each mutator binds `updated_at` as a sub-second-precision *string*, not a datetime, so a regression to the raw binding is caught at the unit layer; the live guard stays the e2e `recovery.spec.ts`). 929 API tests green, `ruff` clean. **KB:** `faq/oltp-to-olap-patterns.md` gains Pattern 8 (the two `updated_at` traps: second-precision `command()` writes losing to microsecond `insert()` writes in the same second, and naive-datetime ambiguity across the two write paths).

This builds them. **API (`api/app/v3/endpoints/recovery.py`):** `POST /v3/recovery/request` `{contact}` → send a 6-digit code (Twilio Verify: `channel=sms` for a phone, `channel=email` for an email — one provider for both); `POST /v3/recovery/verify` `{contact, code}` → check the code, return `{accounts:[{username,email}], verify_token}` (an empty account list is valid — the sign-up path); `POST /v3/recovery/complete` `{verify_token, username, new_password?}` → validate the verify_token, confirm the picked account carries the contact (defense in depth → `CONTACT_NOT_LINKED`), create the account if new (carrying the verified contact; a random password when none is set, so the contact is the credential), optionally set the password (the password-change path), mark the contact verified, mint the login JWT. **The verify_token is the gate** — a short-lived (5-min) signed JWT minted by `verify`; `complete` can't mint a token without it, so a raw `{contact, username}` can't sign in. **Data (`services/clickhouse.py`):** `get_users_by_contact` (phone OR email → all active users on that contact, deduped to the latest row per username). **Twilio (`services/twilio.py`):** `send_verification`/`check_verification` are now channel-aware (sms vs email from the contact) — one provider for both. **Node policy (D10):** `require_contact` node-config flag (`models/config.py` + `services/config.py`); when on, `POST /v3/signup` requires a phone or email (401 `CONTACT_REQUIRED`). web10.app turns it on; a small node can leave it off. **Exceptions:** `BAD_CONTACT`, `CONTACT_REQUIRED`, `CONTACT_NOT_LINKED`. **UI (`ui/`):** the ForgotForm is now the contact flow — a single phone-OR-email input (replacing the phone-only `react-phone-input-2`), the verify_token plumbing, a "New account" option in the pick step (type a username to create), and the "create account" path when no account is on the contact. The login screen gains a prominent "Sign in with phone or email" primary CTA (the username+password form stays as the fallback for accounts without a contact — e2e-safe, `login-submit` unchanged). **Tests:** 23 API (`test_recovery.py` — request/verify/complete, contact mismatch, bad/expired/wrong-purpose verify_token, bad username, the signup contact gate) + 15 UI (`recoveryFlow.test.tsx` — the contact/code/pick/create state machine) + the `test_v3_endpoints` signup test re-aligned (the signup now reads config). 941 API + 164 UI tests green, `tsc` + `ruff` clean. **Note for the operator:** the Twilio Verify service must have the **email channel enabled** in the Twilio Console (a config toggle, not code) before email sign-in delivers end-to-end; phone (sms) works with the existing service. Age assurance (the 2024–2026 legal wave) is a separate, layerable gate — neither phone nor email proves age.

Instead of an app guessing from status codes (a `401` on this node means bad token **or** no permission **or** user-not-found — the information is destroyed at the boundary), the node is the oracle: it runs the actual checks and returns a typed verdict + ordered recovery actions. **API (`POST /v3/session/verify`):** the server runs the real checks — token decode (incl. the custom `expires` claim PyJWT ignores), user lookup, app-contract check (against the request Origin), followers-group membership — and reports each as a stable code. The load-bearing rule (**definite NO vs. UNKNOWN**): a store that is UNREADABLE yields `unknown` (no action), a store that is readable and EMPTY yields the decisive negative (action). A deploy window must not look like "contract missing" — that is what keeps a transient blip from churning every user into a re-auth loop. `status`: `invalid` > `degraded` > `inconclusive` > `ok`. `actions`: `reauth` / `heal_followers_group` / `signout` (decisive problems only; `reauth` before `heal` since the heal needs a live session; `signout` is terminal — a deleted account can't be re-authed). **SDK:** `w.verifySession()` + the `SessionVerdict`/`SessionAction` types. **App (SessionGuard, `src/data/session.ts`):** `verifyAndRecover()` executes the verdict's actions with a 5-min **cooldown** (the loop-breaker — the system tries once, then hands the user the wheel via a "Log in again" banner). `reauth` is **replace-on-arrival** (the handed-back token overwrites the stale cookie; it never clears-then-restores, so a blocked popup can't strand the user signed-out). Wired into `App.tsx`: on mount (`allowReauth:false` — no popup on page load; the safe local heal + terminal signout still run) and on a reactive `401`/`403` data failure (`allowReauth:true` — re-ask the oracle and act). A transient "oracle unreachable" is a `console.warn` (retry-later), not an error. **E2E (`session-verify.spec.ts`):** the dirty-node seatbelt the fresh-node e2e can't provide. API floor seeds each bad state against a real node and asserts the verdict (healthy/`ok`, contract `missing`/`partial`/`reauth`, group `not_member`/`missing`/`heal`, malformed/`missing` token/`reauth`). Browser gauntlet drives the real app through the one recovery that needs no popup (the group heal) and asserts the guard healed the state (membership flips to `ok`, a fresh load renders). **Tests:** 17 API (every verdict code) + 4 SDK + 14 SessionGuard (each action, cooldown, inconclusive no-op, replace-not-strand, mount reauth deferral) + 8 e2e. 832 api + 94 sdk + 249 social (tsc clean) + 249 e2e all green.

the only real role check is a flat `permission in role.permissions` that gates group-management ops only, while document CRUD is gated by the app contract; (2) `anon` is a misnomer — it means "no token" but the grant it carries applies to *any* non-member, signed in or not; (5) the KB contradicts itself (`overview.md` "one role per member" vs `identity.md` "multiple roles per user"; the code is one-role-per-member). **The decision (D58):** roles become **per-service permission maps** (`{name, permissions: {service: [ops]}}` — the same shape the app contract already uses; the `services` array is retired); access is granted to three **nested principal classes** `anyone` / `authenticated` / `member` (retiring `anon`; not `all` — collides with the `*` service wildcard) stored as **reserved keys in `group_members`** (no new table — the discover board's `anon` row becomes the `anyone` row); a principal's effective role is the **union** of the grants on every class they belong to (the nesting enforces member ⊇ signed-in-stranger ⊇ signed-out-visitor for free); **reads are role-gated for content, identity stays public** (the group's face is always visible; the Facebook front door depends on it); **public/private = a role grant to `anyone`/`authenticated`** (no new flag; join policy stays orthogonal); management ops live under the reserved `'group'` service key; **one role per person** (already the code — the per-service map makes it fully expressive). Closes the attach hole for free (the write side gets the same per-service gate). ClickHouse makes it cheap: the role check runs on the small metadata tables → computes the `group_ids` the reader's effective role clears per service → the columnar scan is unchanged. **The KB (the real work of this bite):** new `groups/access.md` (the canonical model reference — the two trust layers, the role shape, principal classes, union semantics, the gates, public/private, worked examples, invariants); `identity.md` / `overview.md` / `discoverability.md` / `social-contracts.md` / `requests.md` / `detail.md` all re-aligned to the per-service map shape + principal classes (the "service-scoped roles" + "multiple roles per user" fiction retired; `anon`-as-member → `anyone`/`authenticated` grants; membership-gate → effective-role-gate throughout). **Version:** stays **v3** (operator: v3 is pre-prod, a month in development — a breaking protocol change stays on the 3.x line, no v4). **Implementation is queued** (not this bite) as the `group-access-model` (D58) lane in `parallel-execution.md` + a new section in `plan.md`: API role shape + read/write gates + backfill + identity write endpoint, conformance re-pin, UI public/private + profile editor, app role definitions, e2e public/private gauntlet. Operator (screenshot): "i tried uploading a profile photo, it gives me error … the whole profile page is extremely broken! i cant even change my name / website." **Three stacked bugs, one screen.** (1) **The upload crash (the screenshot's red banner).** `uploadMedia` (posts.ts) mapped `confirmMediaUpload`'s response through `fromV3DocToMedia` — but the API's `media/confirm` returned a flat `{doc_id, **metadata}`, not a document envelope: `doc.body` was `undefined`, so `body.url` threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'url')`, caught by the upload handler and rendered as the error. On top of that the file was never actually uploaded — the v3 `uploadMedia` skipped the presigned flow entirely ("For now, store the file URL directly — the presigned upload flow will be wired when the v3 media endpoints are fully available"; they've been available since 3.6.0), so even a clean confirm produced a media doc with no blob and no URL. (2) **The avatar never resolves on reload.** `media/list` returned `{doc_id, metadata, created_at}` (also not an envelope) → `resolveMediaRefs`' `fromV3DocToMedia` threw → swallowed by `loadData`'s catch → empty mediaMap → the fallback letter avatar forever. `refreshMediaUrls` also read via `readById(id, 'media')` — a group-scoped read filtered on `collection_name = 'media'`, but the media doc is `media_metadata` with no group → silent 404 → the stale record. (3) **Name/website "doesn't persist."** `saveProfile` wrote the profile doc into the followers group without ensuring it existed — the write 200s (attach doesn't validate group existence) but the next read 403s (not a member), so `readProfile` fell back to the username-only profile and the edit appeared lost. `settings.ts` got exactly this fix in 3.25.3; `profile.ts` was the named "remaining sibling" and was never fixed. **The fixes.** API — `confirm_media_upload` + `list_media` now return the standard document envelope (the metadata is the doc's `body`, same shape as create/read — the SDK's `V3Document` type was the contract all along; the API was the drifted side); `list_media` gains an optional `doc_ids` filter (exact-ref resolution — a bare latest-N list misses avatar refs older than the window); `resolve_media_urls` (the read path) now mints a FRESH presigned `read_url` from the metadata's `object_key` on every read (document-typing: the document never stores a live URL — a legacy stored `url` is only the fallback), and the resolved ref carries the `doc_id` + the real `object_key` (it was putting the doc_id in the `object_key` field). SDK — `listMedia` accepts `doc_ids`. App — `uploadMedia` is now the real three-step flow (presigned POST form → upload the file to MinIO → confirm with the `object_key`, never a URL; the thumbnail's key rides as `thumbnail_object_key`); `refreshMediaUrl(s)` presigns via `getMediaReadUrl(object_key)` (fresh URL, degrades to the record on failure); `resolveMediaRefs` handles the dual ref shape — resolved objects from the API read path map straight to `MediaRecord` (the ONLY cross-user media path — `listMedia` is owner-scoped), string doc_ids resolve via `listMedia(doc_ids)` + presign; `mediaRefId` normalizes ref→doc_id at every `mediaMap` indexing site (UserProfileScreen, ProfileScreen, PostLightbox, DiscoverScreen); `saveProfile` calls `ensureFollowers` before writing (the 3.25.3 settings pattern); the avatar/banner file input is now a PERSISTENT hidden input (`[data-testid="profile-file-input"]`) — the createElement-on-click input was unreachable from Playwright, which is why the upload seam had never been e2e-driven. `[social-media]`/`[profile]` seam logs at every step (kept). **Tests.** API — `TestMedia` re-aligned to the envelope (confirm + list) + new `doc_ids` filter pins + `TestResolveMediaUrls` gains the fresh-presign-from-object_key + legacy-fallback + doc_id/object_key-field pins; `TestMediaConfirm`/`TestMediaList` endpoint pins. SDK — `listMedia` doc_ids (present + empty-omitted). App — new `media.test.ts` (11 tests) drives the REAL data-layer functions (mocked client + fetch): the presigned flow (form → FormData POST → confirm with object_key), the failed-upload throw (no confirm after a 400), the thumbnail recursion, the presign refresh (+thumbnail, legacy no-op, failure degrade), and the dual-shape `resolveMediaRefs` (string→listMedia(doc_ids)+presign, resolved→direct, mixed, empty). B is exact (no staleness), race-free (a read-modify-write counter is not atomic in ClickHouse → lost updates), needs no backfill, and touches no write path; it matches the house's own 3.15.0 "metric-as-query, no maintained counters" precedent. The counter table remains a clean v2 trigger if the board ever outgrows the read-time scan. **ClickHouse gotcha:** the board base's `doc_id` collides with `doc_groups.doc_id`, so ClickHouse names the subquery column `p.doc_id` (qualified) and `b.doc_id` won't resolve through the alias — the fix is an explicit `p.doc_id AS doc_id`. **Degenerate all-zero sort:** v0 scored every post 0 and the stable sort preserved created_at DESC; the SQL falls back to a chronological `ORDER BY` to match. **Tests:** the mocked `TestPowerMeanRead` tests are re-aligned to the single-query shape (query shape, params, row mapping — a mock can't verify the SQL math). The ranking math is proven by a real-ClickHouse equivalence check (`.context/verify_power_mean_sql.py`, run against a live CH): the SQL score matches `_power_mean_score` to ≤1e-9 over a 175-input × 6-sort-config grid, and the full ranked query orders a realistic board correctly (most-loved, newest, balanced-vs-Python, paging tiles the full order). 771 API tests green (1 pre-existing `test_change_pass` passlib/bcrypt env failure, red on `origin/dev` too), ruff check + format clean.

No Celery, no Redis — the node targets a one-container deploy, and the job interface (in, manifest out) doesn't change if a node ever outgrows it. `POST /v3/media/transcode` queues the job (404 not-author — no existence leak, 400 no-video-ref, idempotent while processing). (2) **bifurcated auth** (`services/hls.py`, per `minio-auth-bifurcated.md`) — presigned URLs for everything EXCEPT video: a read of a transcoded doc mints a 10-min JWT (sig) bound to (reader, doc, hls prefix) and injects `transcoding_settings.manifest_url`; the manifest endpoint verifies the sig AND re-checks access (author or group membership) — the expiry is the re-check cadence, so a revoked membership stops the stream within one TTL. The master manifest is synthesized from `transcoding_settings.variants` (the document is the source of truth, the manifest is a view); variant manifests rewrite every segment to a signed URL; segments stream from MinIO sig-only (no DB — the prefix rides in the sig, so a sig for doc X can only address X's HLS tree; variant/seg are regex-locked, traversal → 400). `GET /v3/media/hls/{manifest,variant,segment}`. (3) reads mint the manifest URL (`endpoints/documents.py`); `get_document_any_author` for the re-check; settings: `HLS_RENDITIONS` / `HLS_SIG_TTL` / `HLS_WORKER_CONCURRENCY` / `HLS_FFMPEG_TIMEOUT`; Dockerfile gains ffmpeg + ffprobe. 3.4.2 || 23.08.2026
fix(api) + fix(auth-ui): the auth popup's "Checking node status..." no longer hangs for seconds on login — the API was serializing the popup's burst of concurrent calls on a blocked event loop. Two fixes, both important: (1) **the API stopped blocking the event loop.** Every v3 endpoint (and the `/ready` health check) was `async def` but did purely synchronous work — a blocking `clickhouse_connect` call — so each request held the single-threaded asyncio loop for the duration of its ClickHouse round-trip, and the popup's burst of ~6 concurrent calls (`list`/`list`/`manages`/`profile`/`admin`/`ready`) got *serialized*: total time ≈ the sum of all the round-trips, not the max. The `/ready` request (which "Checking node status..." waits on) was stuck in that queue. Now the endpoints are `def` (sync), so FastAPI runs them in a thread pool and the ClickHouse calls run off the loop; the singleton ClickHouse client is now a **thread-local** (each worker thread gets its own connection, created once on first use) so concurrent requests run in parallel without racing on a shared single connection. (2) **the auth app's burst was collapsed.** On load/login `servicesLoad` was re-triggered by two `useEffect`s (`authTick`, `acrTick`) *and* `finishLogin`, and `checkAdmin` was re-triggered too — so each of `list`/`manages`/`profile`/`admin` fired 4–8× (the flurry in the DevTools screenshot). `servicesLoad` and `checkAdmin` are now debounced (50ms, `useRef` so the timer survives re-renders), collapsing the burst into one call each. Verified: a signed-in popup load now fires exactly one of each call (was ~20), and 6 concurrent `/ready` calls run in parallel (was serialized). New `e2e/tests/concurrency-torture.spec.ts` locks in the fix as an anti-test: a burst of 50 concurrent reads must all succeed with correct data (no 500s/timeouts), and concurrent reads for 8 different users must not cross-contaminate (the thread-local ClickHouse client holds up). NOTE on the test design: a *timing* assertion ("parallel is faster than serialized") was measured and rejected — at N=20–60 a concurrent burst is NOT reliably faster than sequential (a single local ClickHouse serializes the queries, HTTP caps at ~6 connections/host, each worker thread sets up its own connection; speedup 0.9–1.2×), so any timing threshold is flaky by construction (a corrupted measure). Correctness-under-concurrency is the robust, physical signal. This is why it felt like "inconsistent ClickHouse performance" — it was N serialized blocking calls whose sum varied with the network, not ClickHouse being slow. NOTE: pre-existing flaky `authenticator-torture` logout-fork test (parallel-load timing; passes in isolation) is unrelated to this change.

fix(auth-ui): the cross-origin consent handshake actually works now. 3.0.57's "Window-safe replacer" was a no-op — JSON.stringify reads `value.toJSON` BEFORE any replacer runs, and that read throws a SecurityError on a cross-origin Window, so the `normalized contracts` log still aborted the message handler and `setPendingContracts` never ran (popup showed "You're all set" with zero contracts; user was never asked to approve). Two real fixes: (1) `toLogString()` strips `_windowSource` before serializing — used on both the normalize log and the approveContract GCR log; (2) `sendContractResponse` used `windowSource instanceof Window`, which is false cross-origin (different realm prototype), so the approval response was silently dropped — now `typeof windowSource.postMessage === 'function'`. Notes demo now calls `closeAuthPopup()` after the group contract so the window closes (it sent the token but waited forever for a `close_popup` the demo never sent). New aggressive e2e spec `e2e/tests/auth-popup-roundtrip.spec.ts` drives the REAL popup (signed-out demo, no pre-granted contract): asserts the contract renders, approve posts the response, the token lands, the group contract renders, and the popup closes — with both-sides console + pageerror dumps on failure. This is the integration layer the pre-seeded API specs (notes/hello-demo) never covered; it was red on the old code and is green now. docs(ai-use-theory): Step 3 gains the seam rule, the test ladder (gradually harder), and the trust rule (changelog must not claim coverage the code lacks).
